# Simple Computer Adaptive Test (CAT): Two-Stage Branching Quiz

## Metadata

- Framework: Computer Adaptive Test (CAT)
    
- Complexity: Intermediate
    
- Primary Function: Assessment (adaptive quiz delivery + scoring)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: RADIO, JUMP, MAP, EVAL, SET, TN
    
- Key Concepts: Pipe-delimited item parameters, deterministic branching, score accumulation, UI input capture
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Static quizzes can’t adapt difficulty in real time; this agent implements a minimal CAT-style pathway that routes the user to a harder or easier follow-up item based on the first response.
    
- Core Mechanism: A hidden symbolic “router” turn evaluates correctness using EVAL and immediately redirects execution using MAP + JUMP to either the hard path or easy path, then converges on a final score display.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{  
"options": {  
"title": "Simple Computer Adaptive Test (CAT)",  
"brief": "A simple 2-stage adaptive quiz where the difficulty of the next question is determined by the user's answer.",  
"name": "Simple CAT Agent (English)",  
"description": "This agent simulates a simple computer adaptive test (CAT) by dynamically branching to a harder or easier question based on the user's answer to the first question.",  
"greeting": "Welcome to the Simple Adaptive Test. Please answer the first question.",  
"params": {  
"SCORE": {  
"org": "0",  
"cond": "SELF",  
"desc": "The user's initial score."  
},  
"MEDIUM_Q": {  
"org": "What is 5 * 5?|20|25|30|25",  
"cond": "SELF",  
"desc": "A medium-difficulty question with a stem, 3 options, and the correct answer."  
},  
"HARD_Q": {  
"org": "What is the square root of 144?|10|12|14|12",  
"cond": "SELF",  
"desc": "A hard-difficulty question with a stem, 3 options, and the correct answer."  
},  
"EASY_Q": {  
"org": "What is 2 + 2?|3|4|5|4",  
"cond": "SELF",  
"desc": "An easy-difficulty question with a stem, 3 options, and the correct answer."  
}  
}  
},  
"prompts": [  
{  
"user": "/ Turn 1: Display the medium-difficulty question.\n@RADIO("ans_medium", "@MEDIUM_Q[1]@", "@MEDIUM_Q[2:4]@")@",  
"show": true,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"user": "/ Turn 2: Evaluate the user's answer and branch to the correct/incorrect path.\n@JUMP(@MAP("@EVAL("@RADIO(ans_medium)@ == @MEDIUM_Q[5]@")@", "true", "@TN(1)@|@TN(4)@")@)@",  
"show": false,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"user": "/ Turn 3: [Correct Path] Update the score for getting the medium question right.\n@SET(SCORE, "@EVAL("@SCORE@ + 2")@")@",  
"show": false,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"user": "/ Turn 4: [Correct Path] Display the hard-difficulty question.\n@RADIO("ans_hard", "@HARD_Q[1]@", "@HARD_Q[2:4]@")@",  
"show": true,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"user": "/ Turn 5: [Correct Path] Update the score for the hard question.\n@SET(SCORE, "@EVAL("@SCORE@ + @MAP("@EVAL("@RADIO(ans_hard)@ == @HARD_Q[5]@")@", "true", "3|0")@")@")@",  
"show": false,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"user": "/ Turn 6: [Correct Path] Jump to the final result turn.\n@JUMP(@TN(3)@)@",  
"show": false,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"user": "/ Turn 7: [Incorrect Path] Display the easy-difficulty question.\n@RADIO("ans_easy", "@EASY_Q[1]@", "@EASY_Q[2:4]@")@",  
"show": true,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"user": "/ Turn 8: [Incorrect Path] Update the score for the easy question.\n@SET(SCORE, "@EVAL("@SCORE@ + @MAP("@EVAL("@RADIO(ans_easy)@ == @EASY_Q[5]@")@", "true", "1|0")@")@")@",  
"show": false,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"user": "/ Turn 9: Display the final score.\nTest Complete! Your final adaptive score is @SCORE@.",  
"show": true,  
"markdown": true,  
"model": null  
}  
]  
}

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params)

- SCORE: Scalar numeric string initialized to "0"; updated deterministically via @SET() + @EVAL() and displayed at the end.
    
- MEDIUM_Q / HARD_Q / EASY_Q: Pipe-delimited item “records” encoded as a single string:
    

- Index [1]: stem/question text
    
- Slice [2:4]: three options (2,3,4) passed into @RADIO()
    
- Index [5]: correct answer used for correctness checks
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array)

- Turn 1 (Symbolic): Medium item display
    

- Uses @RADIO("ans_medium", stem, options)@ to collect structured user input.
    

- Turn 2 (Symbolic, hidden): Router / branching decision
    

- Computes correctness with @EVAL("@RADIO(ans_medium)@ == @MEDIUM_Q[5]@")@ and maps "true" to a relative jump target via @TN(); then enforces the branch with @JUMP() (router pattern).
    

- Turn 3 (Symbolic, hidden): Correct path scoring for medium item
    

- Adds 2 points to SCORE.
    

- Turn 4 (Symbolic): Hard item display (correct path)
    

- Collects ans_hard via @RADIO().
    

- Turn 5 (Symbolic, hidden): Hard item scoring
    

- Uses nested @MAP(@EVAL(...), "true", "3|0")@ to award 3 points if correct, else 0.
    

- Turn 6 (Symbolic, hidden): Convergence jump
    

- Jumps forward to the final result turn, skipping the easy-path turns.
    

- Turn 7 (Symbolic): Easy item display (incorrect path)
    

- Collects ans_easy via @RADIO().
    

- Turn 8 (Symbolic, hidden): Easy item scoring
    

- Awards 1 point if correct, else 0.
    

- Turn 9 (Symbolic): Final result
    

- Displays @SCORE@ as the final adaptive score.
    

## Visualization Mermaid Code

graph TD

  A[Start: Greeting] --> B[Turn 1 (Symbolic): RADIO ans_medium from MEDIUM_Q]

  B --> C[Turn 2 (Symbolic/Hidden): EVAL correctness + MAP to jump target + JUMP]

  

  C -->|Correct| D[Turn 3 (Hidden): SET SCORE = SCORE + 2]

  D --> E[Turn 4 (Symbolic): RADIO ans_hard from HARD_Q]

  E --> F[Turn 5 (Hidden): SET SCORE += (ans_hard correct ? 3 : 0)]

  F --> G[Turn 6 (Hidden): JUMP to Turn 9]

  

  C -->|Incorrect| H[Turn 7 (Symbolic): RADIO ans_easy from EASY_Q]

  H --> I[Turn 8 (Hidden): SET SCORE += (ans_easy correct ? 1 : 0)]

  I --> J[Turn 9 (Symbolic): Display final SCORE]

  

  G --> J

# Generative AI-based Multi-Stage Assessment (GAMSA) - Item Version: Adaptive Item Routing + Dual-Stage Feedback

## Metadata

- Framework: GAMSA (symbolic mechanics + final LLM synthesis turn; adaptive routing achieved via symbolic state + dynamic indirection)
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Formative Assessment (adaptive item delivery + performance level assignment + narrative tutoring)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: SET, RADIO, EVAL, MAP
    
- Key Concepts: Dynamic parameter indirection (@@...@@), linked parameter alignment (cond: LINK(...)), score-to-level mapping, dual-stage feedback (symbolic summary → LLM narrative)
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Standard adaptive quizzes often stop at right/wrong scoring; this agent adds a second-layer diagnostic experience by storing per-item evidence and producing both an objective summary and an LLM “AI Tutor” narrative report.
    
- Core Mechanism: Each item is graded symbolically (score increment + correctness label), the next item’s parameter name is computed and stored (Q2/Q3 routing), a performance level + canned feedback is derived from the final score, then a final LLM turn synthesizes all stored results into structured tutoring feedback.

"show": false, "model": null  
},

{  
"user": "/ T5: Grade Q2 & Store Results\n@SET(CURRENT_SCORE, "@EVAL("@CURRENT_SCORE@ + @MAP("@EVAL("@RADIO(ans_q2)@ == @@Q2_PARAM_NAME@[5]@")@", "true", "1|0")@")@")@\n@SET(Q3_PARAM_NAME, "@MAP("@EVAL("@RADIO(ans_q2)@ == @@Q2_PARAM_NAME@[5]@")@", "true", "VERY_HARD_Q|VERY_EASY_Q")@")@\n@SET(Q2_TEXT, "@@Q2_PARAM_NAME@[1]@")@\n@SET(Q2_USER_ANS, "@RADIO(ans_q2)@")@\n@SET(Q2_CORRECT_ANS, "@@Q2_PARAM_NAME@[5]@")@\n@SET(Q2_RESULT, "@MAP("@EVAL("@RADIO(ans_q2)@ == @@Q2_PARAM_NAME@[5]@")@", "true", "Correct|Incorrect")@")@",

{ "user": "/ T6: Ask Q3\n@RADIO("ans_q3", "@@Q3_PARAM_NAME@[1]@", "@@Q3_PARAM_NAME@[2:4]@")@", "show": true, "model": null },

"user": "/ T7: Grade Q3 & Store Results\n@SET(CURRENT_SCORE, "@EVAL("@CURRENT_SCORE@ + @MAP("@EVAL("@RADIO(ans_q3)@ == @@Q3_PARAM_NAME@[5]@")@", "true", "1|0")@")@")@\n@SET(Q3_TEXT, "@@Q3_PARAM_NAME@[1]@")@\n@SET(Q3_USER_ANS, "@RADIO(ans_q3)@")@\n@SET(Q3_CORRECT_ANS, "@@Q3_PARAM_NAME@[5]@")@\n@SET(Q3_RESULT, "@MAP("@EVAL("@RADIO(ans_q3)@ == @@Q3_PARAM_NAME@[5]@")@", "true", "Correct|Incorrect")@")@",

"show": true, "markdown": true, "model": "gpt-4.1-nano"  
}  
]  
}

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params)

- INITIAL_SCORE: Session starting scalar (string "0"), copied into the session variable CURRENT_SCORE at runtime.
    
- PERFORMANCE_LEVELS: Pipe list of 4 user-facing labels. Used as an indexed lookup in Turn 8.
    
- LEVEL_FEEDBACK: Pipe list aligned to PERFORMANCE_LEVELS via cond: LINK(PERFORMANCE_LEVELS) (ensures index-consistent pairing across the two lists).
    
- AI_TUTOR_PERSONA: System prompt persona used only in the final LLM synthesis turn (Turn 10).
    
- VERY_EASY_Q / EASY_Q / MEDIUM_Q / HARD_Q / VERY_HARD_Q: Pipe-delimited item “records”:
    

- [1] stem, [2:4] options, [5] correct answer (where present).
    

- Dynamic indirection pattern: @@Q2_PARAM_NAME@[...]@ and @@Q3_PARAM_NAME@[...]@ dereference a parameter name stored in state to retrieve the chosen item’s fields at runtime. This matches CAFA’s documented @@...@@ indirection approach for dynamic retrieval.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array)

- Turn 1 (Symbolic, hidden): Session score initialization
    

- @SET(CURRENT_SCORE, "@INITIAL_SCORE@")@ creates the session score variable.
    

- Turn 2 (Symbolic, visible): Baseline item (Q1)
    

- @RADIO() collects selected-response input and pauses for submission.
    

- Turn 3 (Symbolic, hidden): Grade Q1 + route Q2 + store evidence
    

- Grades correctness using @EVAL() and awards 1|0 via @MAP(); stores the next item’s parameter name in Q2_PARAM_NAME; stores Q1 text, user answer, correct answer, and “Correct/Incorrect”. (This is the core “evidence capture” turn.)
    

- Turn 4 (Symbolic, visible): Adaptive item (Q2) via dynamic parameter name
    

- Uses @@Q2_PARAM_NAME@ to select HARD_Q or EASY_Q and present it via @RADIO().
    

- Turn 5 (Symbolic, hidden): Grade Q2 + route Q3 + store evidence
    

- Same pattern as Turn 3; sets Q3_PARAM_NAME to VERY_HARD_Q or VERY_EASY_Q based on Q2 correctness.
    

- Turn 6 (Symbolic, visible): Adaptive item (Q3) via dynamic parameter name
    

- Uses @@Q3_PARAM_NAME@ to present the third item.
    

- Turn 7 (Symbolic, hidden): Grade Q3 + store evidence
    

- Final score increment + stores Q3 evidence fields.
    

- Turn 8 (Symbolic, hidden): Level assignment + canned feedback retrieval
    

- Converts CURRENT_SCORE (0–3) into a 1–4 LEVEL_INDEX using @MAP("@CURRENT_SCORE@", "3|2|1", "1|2|3|4")@ and retrieves PERFORMANCE_LEVEL and LEVEL_FEEDBACK by index. (MAP list-shape rules apply.)
    

- Turn 9 (Symbolic, visible): Results summary
    

- Displays a structured markdown report from the stored evidence + final score + performance level + symbolic feedback.
    

- Turn 10 (LLM, visible): AI Tutor narrative synthesis
    

- System loads AI_TUTOR_PERSONA; user prompt compiles all stored evidence + score + level + initial feedback; LLM outputs a three-section tutoring report.

# AI-Augmented Thematic Analysis Agent: Transcript-to-Themes Pipeline with Evidence and Final Report

## Metadata

- Framework: ASSISI (structured user data capture + downstream AI “investigator” analysis chain)
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Qualitative Data Analysis (thematic analysis workflow automation)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: TEXTAREA, TR, TN
    
- Key Concepts: IMPACT-style multi-turn chaining (turn-to-turn handoff), relative turn addressing with @TR@TN(-k)@@, staged LLM prompt pipeline
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Manual thematic analysis requires time-intensive transcript review, open coding, theme clustering, and quote extraction; this agent reduces mechanical workload by standardizing these steps into a consistent AI-assisted pipeline.
    
- Core Mechanism: Collects a full transcript once, then runs a 5-step LLM chain (summary → open codes → themes → evidence quotes → synthesis) using robust turn-to-turn result references (@TR@TN(-1)@@, etc.) so later stages consume earlier outputs without hardcoding absolute turn numbers.

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params)

- (None) This agent does not pre-define domain parameters; it relies on a single user-supplied transcript captured via @TEXTAREA("transcript", ...)@ and on turn-result references for chaining.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array)

- Turn 1 (Symbolic, visible): Transcript capture
    

- Collects a full anonymized transcript into the transcript input via @TEXTAREA(...)@.
    

- Turn 2 (LLM, visible): Summarization + key concepts
    

- Uses the transcript to produce a concise summary and highlight key concepts for early-stage data reduction.
    

- Turn 3 (LLM, visible): Open coding
    

- Produces initial codes directly from the transcript (line-by-line instruction).
    

- Turn 4 (LLM, visible): Theme generation from codes
    

- Consumes the previous turn’s output using @TR@TN(-1)@@ (relative reference) to cluster codes into themes + definitions.
    

- Turn 5 (LLM, visible): Evidence extraction
    

- Consumes the most recent themes (@TR@TN(-1)@@) plus the original transcript to extract 3–5 direct quotes per theme.
    

- Turn 6 (LLM, visible): Final synthesis report
    

- Assembles a complete report by pulling outputs from multiple earlier turns using relative indexing:
    

- Summary from 4 turns back: @TR@TN(-4)@@
    
- Codes from 3 turns back: @TR@TN(-3)@@
    
- Themes from 2 turns back: @TR@TN(-2)@@
    
- Quotes from 1 turn back: @TR@TN(-1)@@

# RISE Framework Scoring: Multi-Step Essay Scoring with Iterative Critique Loop

## Metadata

- Framework: RISE (Real-time Intra-Self Evaluation) embedded in an IMPACT-style analysis chain
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Assessment (essay analysis + rubric-based scoring + robustness refinement)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: TEXTAREA, TR, TN, REPEAT
    
- Key Concepts: Evidence-first scoring pipeline, relative turn referencing (@TR@TN(-k)@@), loop iteration variable @R_i@ inside REPEAT, multi-perspective critique → aggregation → final evolution
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Single-pass essay scoring is brittle (misses nuance, can be unfair or inconsistent). This agent improves defensibility by (1) building an evidence-backed initial score via structured analysis and (2) running a RISE critique loop to stress-test and refine the grading decision.
    
- Core Mechanism: Turns 1–6 perform deep textual analysis and generate an initial rubric score; Turn 7 sets a 3× REPEAT loop to run the critique turn multiple times; critiques are aggregated and used to produce a refined final score and justification.

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- (None) This agent stores all working state in turn outputs and user inputs (e.g., essay_text) rather than pre-defined params.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic, visible): Essay capture
    

- Uses @TEXTAREA("essay_text", ...)@ to collect the full response text.
    

- Turn 2 (LLM, visible): Summarization & key concepts
    

- Generates a concise overview to ground subsequent analysis.
    

- Turn 3 (LLM, visible): Labeled key points
    

- Produces short argument labels (analysis “atoms”).
    

- Turn 4 (LLM, visible): Structural mapping from key points
    

- Uses robust relative referencing @TR@TN(-1)@@ to consume the prior turn’s output.
    

- Turn 5 (LLM, visible): Evidence extraction
    

- Extracts direct quotes per structural section to make scoring traceable.
    

- Turn 6 (LLM, visible): Initial synthesis + rubric scoring (RISE step: Generation)
    

- Assembles evidence-backed report and produces category scores.
    

- Turn 7 (Symbolic, hidden): Loop setup (RISE step: Loop Setup)
    

- Uses @REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(1)@, 3)@ to execute the critique turn 3 times; REPEAT must be in a dedicated hidden turn.
    

- Turn 8 (LLM, looped): Iterative critique (RISE step: Repetitive Reflection)
    

- Runs 3 times; @R_i@ indicates the iteration number. Each iteration critiques the initial scoring rather than re-grading the essay.
    

- Turn 9 (LLM): Critique aggregation (RISE step: Aggregation)
    

- Consolidates the multiple critiques into a single actionable recommendation set.
    

- Turn 10 (LLM, visible): Final refined score (RISE step: Evolution)
    

- Produces a revised score and justification using: original essay + initial scoring + aggregated critique guidance.

  D --> E[Turn 4 (LLM): Group Key Points into Sections<br/>Input: @TR@TN(-1)@@]

  B --> F[Turn 5 (LLM): Extract Quotes per Section<br/>Inputs: Sections + essay_text]

  C --> G[Turn 6 (LLM): Synthesis + Initial Rubric Score<br/>Inputs: @TR@TN(-4..-1)@@]

  E --> F

  E --> G

  F --> G

  

  G --> H[Turn 7 (Symbolic/Hidden): REPEAT next turn 3×]

  H --> I[Turn 8 (LLM): Critique Initial Scoring (Iteration @R_i@)<br/>Runs 3 times]

  I --> J[Turn 9 (LLM): Aggregate Critiques]

  G --> K[Turn 10 (LLM): Final Refined Score<br/>Inputs: essay_text + initial score + aggregated recs]

  J --> K

  K --> L[End]

  

## Related Questions and Instructions

### Design & Architecture Requests

- Framework Related:  
    “Generate a RISE agent that uses REPEAT to run a critique turn 3 times, then aggregates and evolves the final answer.”
    
- Structure Related:  
    “Build a deep-analysis front-end that passes outputs using @TR@TN(-k)@@ (no hardcoded @TR1@, @TR2@).”
    
- Complexity Related:  
    “Create an advanced assessment agent that produces an evidence-backed score before any self-critique loop.”
    

### Usage & Modification Requests

- To Change Iteration Count (RISE loop):  
    If you want 5 critiques instead of 3, then edit Turn 7 to @REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(1)@, 5)@ (keep it as the only content in that hidden turn).
    
- To Expand the Rubric:  
    If you add a new category (e.g., “Originality”), then update only Turn 6’s rubric text and require a category score + justification; do not change the REPEAT structure.
    
- To Make Critiques More Diverse:  
    If you want explicit lenses, then insert in Turn 8’s system message a rule like “Iteration 1=fairness, 2=rubric adherence, 3=bias risk” keyed off @R_i@.
    

## References

- Choi, J. (2025). RISE Framework Scoring: Multi-Step Essay Scoring with Iterative Critique Loop. In Collective AI on the Foundation AI (CAFA): The pathway of digital transformation of intelligence. CAFA Lab, Inc.

# K-MOBILE Essential: Knowledge-Map Ontology Tutor with Persistent Progress and Adaptive Next-Step Routing

## Metadata

- Framework: Knowledge Map Ontology-Based Intelligent Learning Engine (K-MOBILE)
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Adaptive Learning (diagnosis → targeted practice → performance analysis → progression → saved state)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: LOAD, SAVE, SET, MAP, INDEX, EVAL, TEXTAREA
    
- Key Concepts: Linear Knowledge Map Ontology, persistent log-based resume, edge-case-safe next/previous computation, LLM output constraint via output-values
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Static e-learning forces all learners through the same path and can’t resume adaptively across sessions; this agent tracks a learner’s current concept on a Knowledge Map and adapts the next concept based on performance, saving progress persistently.
    
- Core Mechanism: Load saved level → select current concept (default if empty) → generate a level-specific word problem → capture response → compute next/previous levels symbolically → LLM diagnoses correctness and recommends next level using explicit rules → extract a single valid level name → save to log → confirm next session topic.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{  
"options": {  
"title": "K-MOBILE Math Tutor",  
"brief": "An adaptive learning engine that guides users through a math knowledge map.",  
"name": "K-MOBILE Agent",  
"description": "This agent uses a linear knowledge map to deliver a personalized math learning experience. It diagnoses the user's current level, provides a targeted problem, and adapts the next step based on performance, saving progress along the way.",  
"greeting": "Welcome to your personalized K-MOBILE Math Tutor! Let's pick up where you left off.",  
"params": {  
"KNOWLEDGE_MAP": {  
"org": "Addition|Subtraction|Multiplication|Division|Fractions|Exponents",  
"cond": "SELF",  
"desc": "A linear map of math concepts."  
},  
"TUTOR_PERSONA": {  
"org": "You are an expert AI Math Tutor. Your goal is to assess a user's skill level based on a linear Knowledge Map and guide their learning.",  
"cond": "SELF"  
}  
}  
},  
"prompts": [  
{  
"user": "/ T1: Load existing learning data from the Agent Log into a parameter.\n@SET(EXISTING_LOG, "@LOAD("LOG")@")@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T2: Determine current skill level. A parameter set in one turn (EXISTING_LOG) must be used in a subsequent turn.\n@SET(CURRENT_LEVEL, "@MAP("@EXISTING_LOG@", "", "@KNOWLEDGE_MAP[1]@|@EXISTING_LOG@")@")@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"system": "@TUTOR_PERSONA@\n\nBased on the provided math topic, create one practice word problem. Your output must be ONLY the word problem itself, with no introductory text or conversational filler.",  
"user": "Topic: @CURRENT_LEVEL@",  
"show": true,  
"model": "gpt-4.1-nano",  
"markdown": true,  
"temperature": "0.1",  
"max-tokens": "4000"  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T4: Present the question from the previous turn and get the user's answer using a TEXTAREA.\n@TEXTAREA("user_answer", "@TR@TN(-1)@@")@",  
"show": true  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T5 (Symbolic Logic): Determine previous/next levels before sending to LLM for more reliable logic.\n@SET(CURRENT_INDEX, "@INDEX("@KNOWLEDGE_MAP@", "@CURRENT_LEVEL@")@")@\n@SET(PREVIOUS_LEVEL, "@MAP("@CURRENT_INDEX@", "1", "@KNOWLEDGE_MAP[1]@|@KNOWLEDGE_MAP[@EVAL("@CURRENT_INDEX@ - 1")@]@")@")@\n@SET(NEXT_LEVEL, "@MAP("@CURRENT_INDEX@", "@KNOWLEDGE_MAP[N]@", "@KNOWLEDGE_MAP[@KNOWLEDGE_MAP[N]@]@|@KNOWLEDGE_MAP[@EVAL("@CURRENT_INDEX@ + 1")@]@")@")@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"system": "@TUTOR_PERSONA@\n\nYou will analyze a student's answer to a math problem. Your task is to:\n1. Determine if the student's answer is correct.\n2. Provide brief diagnostic feedback.\n3. Based ONLY on correctness, state the next skill level using the explicit instructions below.\n4. Conclude by stating the specific skill level name that will be saved for their next session.",  
"user": "Please analyze the following:\n\n- Skill Level Tested: @CURRENT_LEVEL@\n- Question Asked: @TR@TN(-3)@@\n- Student's Answer: @TEXTAREA(user_answer)@\n\n---YOUR DECISION MUST FOLLOW THESE RULES---\n- If the student's answer is CORRECT, the next skill level to save is: @NEXT_LEVEL@\n- If the student's answer is INCORRECT, the next skill level to save is: @PREVIOUS_LEVEL@",  
"show": true,  
"model": "gpt-4.1-nano",  
"markdown": true,  
"temperature": "0.1",  
"max-tokens": "4000"  
},  
{  
"system": "Analyze the provided text. Identify the skill level that should be saved for the next session. Your response must be ONLY the single word for that skill level, chosen from the provided Knowledge Map.",  
"user": "Full analysis text:\n@TR@TN(-1)@@",  
"show": false,  
"model": "gpt-4.1-nano",  
"output-values": "@KNOWLEDGE_MAP@",  
"temperature": "0.1",  
"max-tokens": "4000"  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T8: Save the next skill level to the log. The 'false' argument overwrites the log, storing only the current level.\n@SAVE("@TR@TN(-1)@@", "LOG", "false")@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T9: Display a confirmation message with the skill level for the next session.\nYour progress has been saved. Your next session will focus on @TR@TN(-2)@@.",  
"show": true,  
"markdown": true  
}  
]  
}

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- KNOWLEDGE_MAP: Pipe-delimited linear ontology of concepts (indexable list). Used for:
    

- default start level ([1])
    
- current index lookup via @INDEX()@
    
- neighbor computation via @EVAL(index ± 1)@
    
- constrained extraction in the level-normalization turn (output-values)
    

- TUTOR_PERSONA: Shared system persona injected into LLM turns to keep generation + diagnosis consistent.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic, hidden): Persistent state load
    

- Loads "LOG" into EXISTING_LOG using @LOAD()@.
    

- Turn 2 (Symbolic, hidden): Current level diagnosis
    

- If the log is empty, sets CURRENT_LEVEL to the first map node; otherwise uses the saved value via @MAP() defaulting.
    

- Turn 3 (LLM, visible): Targeted item generation
    

- Produces exactly one word problem for CURRENT_LEVEL (output constrained to “problem only” by instruction).
    

- Turn 4 (Symbolic, visible): Response capture
    

- Presents the generated prompt (@TR@TN(-1)@@) inside @TEXTAREA("user_answer", ...)@.
    

- Turn 5 (Symbolic, hidden): Reliable progression computation
    

- Computes CURRENT_INDEX with @INDEX()@, then precomputes PREVIOUS_LEVEL and NEXT_LEVEL with boundary handling (first stays first; last stays last).
    

- Turn 6 (LLM, visible): Diagnosis + rule-bound next level recommendation
    

- LLM evaluates correctness and must choose between the already-computed @NEXT_LEVEL@ or @PREVIOUS_LEVEL@ (explicit decision rule).
    

- Turn 7 (LLM, hidden): Level name normalization (data integrity gate)
    

- Extracts only a single valid skill level token, constrained to values in @KNOWLEDGE_MAP@ via output-values.
    

- Turn 8 (Symbolic, hidden): Persistent save
    

- Writes the chosen level back to "LOG" (overwrite mode "false").
    

- Turn 9 (Symbolic, visible): Confirmation
    

- Displays the next session topic (references the extracted level from Turn 7 via @TR@TN(-2)@@).
    

## Visualization Mermaid Code

graph TD

  A[Start: Greeting] --> B[T1 (Hidden): LOAD LOG -> EXISTING_LOG]

  B --> C[T2 (Hidden): Set CURRENT_LEVEL (default or saved)]

  C --> D[T3 (LLM): Generate word problem for CURRENT_LEVEL]

  D --> E[T4 (Visible): TEXTAREA user_answer showing generated problem]

  E --> F[T5 (Hidden): INDEX + compute PREVIOUS_LEVEL and NEXT_LEVEL]

  F --> G[T6 (LLM): Diagnose + recommend next level by explicit rule]

  G --> H[T7 (Hidden LLM): Extract single level (output-values KNOWLEDGE_MAP)]

  H --> I[T8 (Hidden): SAVE extracted level to LOG (overwrite)]

  I --> J[T9 (Visible): Confirm next session focus]

  J --> B[Next Session: resume from LOG]

  

## Related Questions and Instructions

### Design & Architecture Requests

- Framework Related:  
    “Generate a K-MOBILE learning agent that uses a Knowledge Map and a persistent LOG to resume progress.”
    
- Structure Related:  
    “Create an agent that computes next/previous nodes symbolically (INDEX/EVAL) before sending decisions to the LLM.”
    
- Complexity Related:  
    “Generate an advanced tutor that includes an LLM ‘normalization gate’ constrained by output-values.”
    

### Usage & Modification Requests

- To Add Multi-Student Support:  
    If you want separate progress per learner, then add an early ID capture (e.g., @TEXT("student_id", ...)@) and change LOAD/SAVE targets from "LOG" to "LOG_@TEXT(student_id)@" (same overwrite behavior).
    
- To Add Richer Ontology Per Concept:  
    If you need objectives/templates/resources per node, then replace KNOWLEDGE_MAP with parallel lists (or an encoded record list) and update Turn 3 to pass the node’s template/objectives into the prompt while keeping the same state-save pattern.
    
- To Integrate with GAMSA (testlets):  
    If you want multi-item stages per level, then replace Turn 3–4 with a small item bundle (testlet) generation/admin, and keep Turn 8’s saved value as the knowledge-map node decided after the stage.
    
- To Track Error Types:  
    If you want diagnostic logging, then extend Turn 6 to output a structured error label, and save a combined value (or a second log key) alongside the next level.
    
- To Add Gamification:  
    If you want points/badges, then introduce a separate SCORE log key and update it when NEXT_LEVEL advances; keep level saving unchanged.
    

## References

- Choi, J. (2025). K-MOBILE Essential: Knowledge-Map Ontology Tutor with Persistent Progress and Adaptive Next-Step Routing. In Collective AI on the Foundation AI (CAFA): The pathway of digital transformation of intelligence. CAFA Lab, Inc.

# Profile Manager - Essential: Persistent Multi-User Profile in LOG with Concurrency-Safe Update Pattern

## Metadata

- Framework: MACRO
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Data Collection & Profile Management (persistent create/read/update with user-controlled loop)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: LOAD, SAVE, SET, INDEX, JUMP, MAP, RADIO, TEXT, EVAL, END
    
- Key Concepts: LOG as flat-file database, UID-keyed record lookup, branch routing (new vs returning), modify-then-save separation, re-fetch/re-index for concurrency safety
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Agents often need persistent, per-user state without an external database. This agent implements durable multi-user profiles (Nickname, Level) using the built-in LOG as storage, with safeguards to avoid stale reads during updates.
    
- Core Mechanism: The agent loads LOG → finds the current user’s @UID@ index → branches into New User (append + end) or Returning User (menu loop). Updates always reload LOG and re-index immediately before modifying in-memory data, then save in a separate turn.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{  
"options": {  
"title": "Persistent User Profile Manager",  
"name": "Persistent Profile Manager",  
"brief": "A robust agent that saves user profile data directly to the LOG.",  
"description": "This agent checks if a user exists in the LOG. New users are prompted to create a profile (Nickname, Level), which is appended to the LOG. Returning users can repeatedly update their information until they choose to exit.",  
"greeting": "Welcome to the User Profile System. Let's get started."  
},  
"prompts": [  
{  
"user": "/ T1: Load the entire log from storage into a parameter.\n@SET(LOG_DATA, "@LOAD("LOG")@")@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T2: Find the user's index within the loaded log data.\n@SET(USER_INDEX, "@INDEX("@LOG_DATA@", "@UID@")@")@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T3: Router - Jump to the appropriate path based on whether the user was found.\n@JUMP(@MAP("@USER_INDEX@", "0", "@TN(1)@|@TN(4)@")@)@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T4: [New User Path] Ask for Nickname.\n@TEXT("new_nickname", "It looks like you're new here! What is your nickname?")@",  
"show": true  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T5: [New User Path] Ask for Level.\n@TEXT("new_level", "Thanks! What is your starting level?")@",  
"show": true  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T6: [New User Path] Append the new user's data to the log and end.\n@SAVE("|@UID@|@TEXT(new_nickname)@|@TEXT(new_level)@", "LOG", "true")@\n@END@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T7: [Returning User Path] Extract user's Nickname and Level from the log data.\n@SET(USER_NICKNAME, "@LOG_DATA[@EVAL("@USER_INDEX@+1")@]@")@\n@SET(USER_LEVEL, "@LOG_DATA[@EVAL("@USER_INDEX@+2")@]@")@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T8: [Returning User Path] Main Menu - Greet user and ask what they want to do.\n@RADIO("user_choice", "Hi, @USER_NICKNAME@! (Level: @USER_LEVEL@) What would you like to do?", "Update Nickname|Update Level|Exit")@",  
"show": true  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T9: [Returning User Path] Menu Router - Jump based on user's choice.\n@JUMP(@MAP("@RADIO(user_choice)@", "Update Nickname|Update Level", "@TN(1)@|@TN(4)@|@TN(7)@")@)@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T10: [Update Nickname Path] Ask for the new Nickname.\n@TEXT("updated_nickname", "What should your new nickname be?")@",  
"show": true  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T11: [Update Nickname Path] MODIFY step: Reload, re-index, and update variables in memory.\n@SET(LOG_DATA, "@LOAD("LOG")@")@\n@SET(USER_INDEX, "@INDEX("@LOG_DATA@", "@UID@")@")@\n@SET(USER_NICKNAME, "@TEXT(updated_nickname)@")@\n@SET(LOG_DATA[@EVAL("@USER_INDEX@+1")@], "@TEXT(updated_nickname)@")@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T12: [Update Nickname Path] SAVE step: Save the modified data and return to menu.\n@SAVE("@LOG_DATA@", "LOG", "false")@\n@JUMP(8)@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T13: [Update Level Path] Ask for the new Level.\n@TEXT("updated_level", "What is your new level?")@",  
"show": true  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T14: [Update Level Path] MODIFY step: Reload, re-index, and update variables in memory.\n@SET(LOG_DATA, "@LOAD("LOG")@")@\n@SET(USER_INDEX, "@INDEX("@LOG_DATA@", "@UID@")@")@\n@SET(USER_LEVEL, "@TEXT(updated_level)@")@\n@SET(LOG_DATA[@EVAL("@USER_INDEX@+2")@], "@TEXT(updated_level)@")@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T15: [Update Level Path] SAVE step: Save the modified data and return to menu.\n@SAVE("@LOG_DATA@", "LOG", "false")@\n@JUMP(8)@",  
"show": false  
},  
{  
"user": "/ T16: [Exit Path] Display a farewell message and end the session.\nThank you for visiting. Session ended.\n@END@",  
"show": true  
}  
]  
}

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- (None) This essential agent does not define params. All persistence is stored in the LOG and all session state is held in variables set during execution.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic): Load LOG into memory
    

- @LOAD("LOG")@ is stored in LOG_DATA to ensure all subsequent reads operate on a single snapshot.
    

- Turn 2 (Symbolic): Locate user record
    

- @INDEX("@LOG_DATA@", "@UID@")@ returns the position of the current UID token; 0 signals “not found”.
    

- Turn 3 (Symbolic): New vs Returning router
    

- @MAP(USER_INDEX, "0", "new|returning")@ feeds @JUMP(...)@ to branch.
    

- Turns 4–6 (Symbolic): New user creation (append)
    

- Collects new_nickname and new_level, then appends |UID|Nickname|Level using @SAVE(..., "true")@ and ends.
    

- Turn 7 (Symbolic): Returning user profile extraction
    

- Reads adjacent fields by offset: nickname at USER_INDEX+1, level at USER_INDEX+2.
    

- Turns 8–9 (Symbolic): Menu loop hub + router
    

- @RADIO captures intent; @JUMP(@MAP(...))@ routes to update nickname, update level, or exit.
    

- Turns 10–12 (Symbolic): Update Nickname path (Ask → Modify → Save → Return)
    

- Modify turn (T11) reloads LOG and re-indexes to avoid stale writes, then updates LOG_DATA[USER_INDEX+1].
    
- Save turn (T12) commits the modified LOG_DATA with overwrite @SAVE(..., "false")@, then jumps back to menu (Turn 8).
    

- Turns 13–15 (Symbolic): Update Level path (Ask → Modify → Save → Return)
    

- Same concurrency-safe pattern, but modifies LOG_DATA[USER_INDEX+2].
    

- Turn 16 (Symbolic): Exit
    

- Displays farewell and ends session.
    

## Visualization Mermaid Code

graph TD

  A[Start] --> B[T1: LOAD LOG -> LOG_DATA]

  B --> C[T2: INDEX LOG_DATA for @UID@ -> USER_INDEX]

  C --> D{T3: USER_INDEX == 0 ?}

  

  D -- Yes (New) --> E[T4: TEXT new_nickname]

  E --> F[T5: TEXT new_level]

  F --> G[T6: SAVE append |UID|Nick|Level (true) + END]

  

  D -- No (Returning) --> H[T7: Extract nickname/level via offsets]

  H --> I[T8: RADIO menu]

  I --> J{T9: Route choice}

  

  J -- Update Nickname --> K[T10: TEXT updated_nickname]

  K --> L[T11: MODIFY: reload LOG + re-index + set LOG_DATA[+1]]

  L --> M[T12: SAVE overwrite (false) + JUMP to menu]

  M --> I

  

  J -- Update Level --> N[T13: TEXT updated_level]

  N --> O[T14: MODIFY: reload LOG + re-index + set LOG_DATA[+2]]

  O --> P[T15: SAVE overwrite (false) + JUMP to menu]

  P --> I

  

  J -- Exit --> Q[T16: Farewell + END]

  

## Related Questions and Instructions

### Design & Architecture Requests

- Framework Related:  
    “Generate a agent that uses LOG as a flat-file database and supports update loops.”
    
- Structure Related:  
    “Create a branch router using INDEX + MAP + JUMP for new vs returning users.”
    
- Complexity Related:  
    “Generate an advanced symbolic-only agent with concurrency-safe update steps.”
    

### Usage & Modification Requests

- To Add a New Profile Field (e.g., Email):  
    If you add a third field, then extend the LOG record shape to |UID|Nickname|Level|Email and:
    

- New User Path: add a new @TEXT("new_email", ...)@ turn before the append SAVE.
    
- Returning User Path: update extraction offsets and update paths to target USER_INDEX+3.
    

- To Enforce Input Safety (Reserved Characters):  
    If you must prevent | or @ in user inputs, then insert a validation/sanitization symbolic turn immediately after each @TEXT(...)@ capture and before any @SAVE(...)@ call.
    
- To Change Storage Key (multiple tables):  
    If you want separate logs (e.g., "PROFILE_LOG"), then replace every @LOAD("LOG")@ / @SAVE(..., "LOG", ...)@ with the new key consistently.
    
- To Strengthen Concurrency Safety Further:  
    If you add any new update path, then follow the same 3-turn pattern: Ask → (Reload + Re-index + Modify in memory) → Save in dedicated turn.
    

## References

- Choi, J. (2025). Profile Manager - Essential: Persistent Multi-User Profile in LOG with Concurrency-Safe Update Pattern. In Collective AI on the Foundation AI (CAFA): The pathway of digital transformation of intelligence. CAFA Lab, Inc.

# Socratic Tutor - Essential: Configurable Socratic Dialogue Loop with TN-Based REPEAT and Final Learning Summary

## Metadata

- Framework: RISE (looped reflective dialogue pattern via REPEAT + iteration index @R_i@)
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Instructional Dialogue (Socratic tutoring + final synthesis)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: REPEAT, TN, TR, TU, EVAL
    
- Key Concepts: Symbolic initiation vs main loop separation, Agent Parameters (APs) for configurability, dynamic relative turn references (@TR@TN(-k)@@), loop logging with @R_i@, end-of-loop synthesis
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Generic “tutor chat” agents often lose structure and context over multiple turns; this agent enforces a repeatable Socratic process (analyze → guide via questions → ask next question) while maintaining a structured conversation history for continuity and a final learning summary.
    
- Core Mechanism: A symbolic opening question begins the session, then a REPEAT loop runs the main Socratic exchange for a configurable number of turns, logging each iteration with stable turn indexing, and finishes with a final LLM synthesis using a separate analysis persona.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{  
"options": {  
"title": "Socratic Tutor",  
"name": "Socratic Tutor",  
"description": "An advanced AI tutor that uses a modular design with a symbolic first turn and configurable system prompts.",

"org": "To get started, what is a topic you've been curious about or have found challenging?",

"org": "Role: You are an expert AI tutor specializing in the Socratic method. Your goal is to guide a student's understanding by asking probing questions. Instead of giving direct answers, help the student build their own knowledge by breaking down complex topics and exploring concepts step-by-step. For each turn, your process is:\n1. Analyze: Briefly analyze the student's previous answer for understanding.\n2. Feedback & Guide: Provide encouraging, corrective feedback by asking questions that guide the student to correct their own thinking.\n3. Ask: Conclude with a single, clear, follow-up question to continue the exploration.\n\nYour entire response should be a short analysis followed by the next question.",  
"cond": "SELF",  
"desc": "The detailed system prompt defining the AI's role as a Socratic tutor."  
},

"org": "5",  
"cond": "SELF",

"org": "You are an expert educator. You are provided with a tutoring conversation. Analyze it and provide a 'Learning Summary' with three sections:\n1. Key Concepts Covered\n2. Areas of Strong Understanding\n3. Suggested Next Topics to Explore",  
"cond": "SELF",  
"desc": "The system prompt for the final analysis turn."  
}  
}  
},  
"prompts": [  
{

"show": true,

},

"user": "",

},

"show": false,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"system": "@PERSONA@\n\n- Conversation history:\n@TR@TN(-2)@@\n@TR@TN(1)@@",

"max-tokens": "2000",  
"show": true,

"markdown": true  
},  
{  
"user": "/ This hidden turn logs the conversation history from the previous turn.\nTurn @EVAL("@R_i@ + 1")@ {\n - Student: @TU@TN(-1)@[@R_i@]@\n - Tutor: @TR@TN(-1)@[@R_i@]@\n}",  
"show": false,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"system": "@ANALYSIS_PERSONA@",  
"user": "Please analyze the following tutoring session:\n\n- First Exchange:\n@TR2@\n\n- Subsequent Conversation:\n@TR@TN(-1)@@",  
"temperature": "0.1",  
"max-tokens": "2000",  
"show": true,  
"model": "gpt-4.1-nano",  
"markdown": true  
}  
]  
}

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- Ini_Question: First user-facing prompt. Changing it re-targets the entire tutor’s starting domain without editing turns.
    
- PERSONA: Governs every tutoring response format: Analyze → Guide via questions → Ask one follow-up question.
    
- MAX_TURNS: Session length controller; the loop count is computed as MAX_TURNS - 1 because Turn 2 already completes the first exchange.
    
- ANALYSIS_PERSONA: Dedicated synthesis persona for final “Learning Summary” structure.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic, visible): Initiation question display
    

- Outputs the literal content of @Ini_Question@.
    

- Turn 2 (LLM, visible): First Socratic exchange
    

- user: "" pauses for the student’s first response; the tutor responds under @PERSONA@.
    
- This first exchange is later referenced explicitly as @TR2@.
    

- Turn 3 (Symbolic, hidden): Loop setup using TN and REPEAT
    

- @REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(2)@, @EVAL("@MAX_TURNS@ - 1")@)@ repeats the next two turns (Turn 4 + Turn 5) the remaining number of times.
    

- Turn 4 (LLM, visible; inside loop): Ongoing Socratic dialogue
    

- System includes full history by combining:
    

- initial exchange: @TR@TN(-2)@@ (resolves to Turn 2 output)
    
- accumulated loop history: @TR@TN(1)@@ (resolves to the log turn’s growing content)
    

- user: "" captures the student reply each iteration.
    

- Turn 5 (Symbolic, hidden; inside loop): History logging with iteration index
    

- Appends a structured record:
    

- Student utterance from @TU@TN(-1)@[@R_i@]@
    
- Tutor utterance from @TR@TN(-1)@[@R_i@]@
    

- Labels each entry as Turn @EVAL("@R_i@ + 1")@ to align iteration numbering.
    

- Turn 6 (LLM, visible): Synthesis (Learning Summary)
    

- Uses @ANALYSIS_PERSONA@.
    
- Input includes:
    

- First exchange: @TR2@
    
- Subsequent looped conversation: @TR@TN(-1)@@ (the structured log produced in Turn 5)
    

## Visualization Mermaid Code

graph TD

  A[Start: Greeting] --> B[T1 (Symbolic): Display Ini_Question]

  B --> C[T2 (LLM): First Socratic response (PERSONA)]

  C --> D[T3 (Hidden): REPEAT loop setup (MAX_TURNS - 1)]

  

  D --> E[T4 (LLM, loop): Socratic turn with history<br/>@TR@TN(-2)@@ + @TR@TN(1)@@]

  E --> F[T5 (Hidden, loop): Append log entry<br/>uses @R_i@, @TU, @TR]

  F -. repeat .-> E

  

  D -->|After loop completes| G[T6 (LLM): Learning Summary (ANALYSIS_PERSONA)<br/>Inputs: @TR2@ + log]

  G --> H[End]

  

## Related Questions and Instructions

### Design & Architecture Requests

- Framework Related:  
    “Generate a Socratic tutor agent that uses REPEAT + R_i to run a fixed-length dialogue and ends with a learning summary.”
    
- Structure Related:  
    “Create an agent that separates initiation (one symbolic turn) from the main loop, and uses TN for robust loop addressing.”
    
- Complexity Related:  
    “Generate an advanced dialogue agent that logs each iteration with TU/TR arrays and then synthesizes the session.”
    

### Usage & Modification Requests

- To Change Session Length:  
    Update MAX_TURNS only. The loop count automatically becomes @EVAL("@MAX_TURNS@ - 1")@.
    
- To Change Tutor Behavior Without Editing Turns:  
    Modify PERSONA (e.g., stricter, more encouraging, domain-specific), and optionally replace Ini_Question.
    
- To Change Summary Format:  
    Edit ANALYSIS_PERSONA to alter the sections, while leaving the logging and loop intact.
    
- To Reuse as a Sales/Support Interviewer:  
    Replace PERSONA with a questioning framework for discovery/troubleshooting and keep the same loop + logging pattern.
    

## References

- Choi, J. (2025). Socratic Tutor - Essential: Configurable Socratic Dialogue Loop with TN-Based REPEAT and Final Learning Summary. In Collective AI on the Foundation AI (CAFA): The pathway of digital transformation of intelligence. CAFA Lab, Inc.

# AI-to-AI Monitored Conversation: Two-Agent Simulation with Human Stop/Continue Gate and Supervisory Analysis

## Metadata

- Framework: RISE (looped multi-agent exchange with REPEAT, iteration index @R_i@, and a mid-loop “evaluation gate” via monitor control)
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Simulation & Supervision (AI-to-AI dialogue generation with human monitoring and final analysis)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: TEXTAREA, REPEAT, TN, TR, EVAL, RADIO, MAP, JUMP
    
- Key Concepts: Dual personas (Counselor/Counselee), human-in-the-loop checkpoint, conditional loop break (Stop → jump to analysis), cumulative transcript logging across iterations
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Pure AI-to-AI simulations can run uncontrolled and lose auditability. This agent adds (1) a human monitor checkpoint each turn and (2) deterministic transcript accumulation, enabling supervised simulations for training, testing, and review.
    
- Core Mechanism: The user supplies the Counselee’s initial problem, a @REPEAT loop runs Counselor→Counselee→Monitor→Router→Logger, the monitor can terminate early via “Stop” (breaking out to final analysis), and the full transcript is synthesized by an analysis persona.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{  
"options": {  
"title": "AI Counselor & Counselee Session (Monitored)",  
"name": "AI Counselor Session (Monitored)",  
"description": "An agent that simulates a monitored conversation between an AI Counselor and Counselee, allowing the user to stop or continue the session at each step.",  
"greeting": "Welcome. Please describe the problem or topic you would like the AI Counselee to discuss with the AI Counselor.",  
"params": {  
"COUNSELOR_PERSONA": {  
"org": "You are a thoughtful and empathetic AI Counselor. Your goal is to help the Counselee explore their feelings and thoughts about the problem they are facing. Ask open-ended, insightful, and supportive questions. Do not give advice, but rather guide them to find their own understanding.",  
"cond": "SELF",  
"desc": "Defines the Counselor's persona."  
},  
"COUNSELEE_PERSONA": {  
"org": "You are an AI Counselee. You will be given a problem to discuss. Respond honestly and reflectively to the Counselor's questions. Base your personality and responses on the initial problem description.",  
"cond": "SELF",  
"desc": "Defines the Counselee's persona."  
},  
"MAX_TURNS": {  
"org": "5",  
"cond": "SELF",  
"desc": "The number of back-and-forth exchanges in the session."  
},  
"ANALYSIS_PERSONA": {  
"org": "You are a clinical supervisor reviewing a counseling session. Analyze the full conversation between the Counselor and Counselee. Summarize the key themes discussed, the Counselor's approach, and the Counselee's progress or insights.",  
"cond": "SELF",  
"desc": "The persona for the final analysis of the session."  
}  
}  
},  
"prompts": [  
{  
"user": "/ This turn captures the initial problem from the user.\n@TEXTAREA("counselee_problem", "Please describe the problem for the Counselee:")@",  
"show": true,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"user": "/ This hidden turn sets up the conversation loop.\n@REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(5)@, @MAX_TURNS@)@",  
"show": false,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"system": "@COUNSELOR_PERSONA@",  
"user": "This is a counseling session. Here is the context:\n\n- Initial Problem: "@TEXTAREA(counselee_problem)@"\n\n- Conversation History So Far:\n@TR@TN(4)@[@EVAL("@R_i@-1")@]@\n\nPlease continue the conversation by asking your next question.",  
"temperature": "0.7",  
"max-tokens": "2000",  
"show": true,  
"model": "gpt-4.1-nano",  
"markdown": true  
},  
{  
"system": "@COUNSELEE_PERSONA@",  
"user": "You are in a counseling session. Here is the context:\n\n- Your Initial Problem: "@TEXTAREA(counselee_problem)@"\n\n- Conversation History So Far:\n@TR@TN(3)@[@EVAL("@R_i@-1")@]@\n\n- The Counselor just said to you:\n"@TR@TN(-1)@[@R_i@]@"\n\nPlease provide your response.",  
"temperature": "0.7",  
"max-tokens": "2000",  
"show": true,  
"model": "gpt-4.1-nano",  
"markdown": true  
},  
{  
"user": "/ This turn asks the monitor if the session should continue.\n@RADIO("monitor_choice_@R_i@", "Monitor: Do you want to continue the session?", "Continue|Stop")@",  
"show": true,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"user": "/ This hidden turn acts as a router. If the monitor selects 'Stop', it jumps to the final analysis turn.\n@JUMP(@MAP("@RADIO(monitor_choice_@R_i@)@", "Stop", "@TN(2)@", "")@)@",  
"show": false,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"user": "/ This hidden turn logs the full, cumulative history for the next loop.\n@TR@TN(0)@[@EVAL("@R_i@-1")@]@\n\nTurn @R_i@:\n- Counselor: @TR@TN(-4)@[@R_i@]@\n- Counselee: @TR@TN(-3)@[@R_i@]@",  
"show": false,  
"model": null  
},  
{  
"system": "@ANALYSIS_PERSONA@",  
"user": "Please analyze the following counseling session transcript.\n\n### Initial Problem\n@TEXTAREA(counselee_problem)@\n\n### Full Transcript\n@TR@TN(-1)@@",  
"temperature": "0.1",  
"max-tokens": "4000",  
"show": true,  
"model": "gpt-4.1-nano",  
"markdown": true  
}  
]  
}

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- COUNSELOR_PERSONA: Controls questioning style (empathetic, open-ended, non-advice).
    
- COUNSELEE_PERSONA: Controls reflective respondent behavior anchored to the initial problem.
    
- MAX_TURNS: Upper bound on loop iterations (conversation “budget”).
    
- ANALYSIS_PERSONA: Defines supervisory synthesis format at the end.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic, visible): Scenario seed (human)
    

- Captures the initial counselee problem via @TEXTAREA("counselee_problem", ...)@.
    

- Turn 2 (Symbolic, hidden): Loop setup
    

- @REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(5)@, @MAX_TURNS@)@ repeats Turns 3–7 for up to MAX_TURNS iterations.
    

- Turn 3 (LLM, visible; in loop): Counselor generates next question
    

- Receives initial problem + “conversation so far” (pulled from the logger’s stored history using indexed access with @EVAL("@R_i@-1")@).
    

- Turn 4 (LLM, visible; in loop): Counselee responds
    

- Receives the problem + history + the counselor’s latest utterance and produces a reflective reply.
    

- Turn 5 (Symbolic, visible; in loop): Monitor checkpoint
    

- Human chooses Continue/Stop using a per-iteration key: monitor_choice_@R_i@.
    

- Turn 6 (Symbolic, hidden; in loop): Conditional break router
    

- If Stop, @JUMP(...)@ routes to the final analysis turn; if Continue, execution falls through.
    

- Turn 7 (Symbolic, hidden; in loop): Transcript accumulator
    

- Appends the latest counselor + counselee lines to the cumulative transcript for the next iteration’s context.
    

- Turn 8 (LLM, visible): Supervisory analysis
    

- Uses ANALYSIS_PERSONA to summarize themes, counselor approach, and counselee progress, consuming the fully accumulated transcript.

graph TD

  A[Start] --> B[T1 (Symbolic): TEXTAREA counselee_problem]

  B --> C[T2 (Hidden): REPEAT loop setup (Turns 3–7) up to MAX_TURNS]

  

  C --> D[T3 (LLM): Counselor asks next question<br/>Inputs: problem + prior transcript]

  D --> E[T4 (LLM): Counselee responds<br/>Inputs: problem + transcript + last counselor line]

  E --> F[T5 (Symbolic): Monitor RADIO Continue/Stop]

  F --> G{T6 (Hidden): If Stop?}

  G -- Continue --> H[T7 (Hidden): Append counselor+counselee to cumulative transcript]

  H --> D

  

  G -- Stop --> I[T8 (LLM): Supervisory analysis (ANALYSIS_PERSONA)]

  C -->|Loop ends naturally| I

  I --> J[End]

  

## Related Questions and Instructions

### Design & Architecture Requests

- Framework Related:  
    “Generate a monitored AI-to-AI simulation agent with a human Continue/Stop gate each iteration.”
    
- Structure Related:  
    “Create a two-persona REPEAT loop where each persona sees the cumulative transcript and produces the next turn.”
    
- Complexity Related:  
    “Build an advanced multi-agent loop that can be terminated early with MAP+JUMP and ends with a supervisor summary.”
    

### Usage & Modification Requests

- To Change the Intervention Frequency:  
    If you want the monitor checkpoint every 2 turns instead of every turn, then move the RADIO + router turns to run conditionally (e.g., only when @EVAL("@R_i@ % 2")@ matches) while keeping the transcript logger in every iteration.
    
- To Add a Second Monitor Action (e.g., “Rewrite last counselor question”):  
    If you add a third option, then extend the MAP/JUMP router to branch to a corrective path turn before logging.
    
- To Reuse for Sales/Support/Negotiation:  
    Replace COUNSELOR_PERSONA/COUNSELEE_PERSONA with the two target roles and keep the same monitor gate + logging + analysis structure.
    
- To Make the Transcript More Structured:  
    If you want JSON logs, then change Turn 7’s formatting to a consistent JSON-like record per Turn @R_i@ (do not change REPEAT bounds).
    

## References

- Choi, J. (2025). AI-to-AI Monitored Conversation: Two-Agent Simulation with Human Stop/Continue Gate and Supervisory Analysis. In Collective AI on the Foundation AI (CAFA): The pathway of digital transformation of intelligence. CAFA Lab, Inc.

# Interactive Questionnaire & AI Analysis: ASSISI-Based Survey and Real-Time Synthesis

## Metadata

- Framework: ASSISI (AI-Supported Survey Instrument & Simultaneous Investigator)
    
- Complexity: Intermediate
    
- Primary Function: Data Collection & Diagnostic Analysis
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: SET, RADIO, CHECKBOX, SELECT, TEXT, TEXTAREA
    
- Key Concepts: Structured Survey Instrument, Multi-Control Input, Consolidated Parameter Design, Final-State LLM Analysis
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved:  
    Traditional surveys collect structured data but require separate analytical steps, delaying insight and fragmenting interpretation.
    
- Core Mechanism:  
    This agent implements the ASSISI pattern by collecting all user inputs through symbolic UI controls first, then passing the complete, structured response set into a single LLM turn for simultaneous, holistic analysis.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{

    "options": {

        "title": "Interactive Questionnaire & AI Analysis",

        "brief": "This agent demonstrates various user input controls through an interactive questionnaire and concludes with an AI-generated analysis of the user's responses based on the ASSISI framework.",

        "name": "ASSISI Framework Example",

        "description": "This agent starts with an invisible setup turn to define all questionnaire content in consolidated parameters. It then presents a series of questions using different UI controls. In the final step, all user responses are gathered and sent to an LLM for a comprehensive, real-time analysis.",

        "greeting": "Hello! Please answer the following questions. Once completed, I will provide an AI-generated analysis based on your responses.",

        "params": {}

    },

    "prompts": [

        {

            "user": "/ This hidden turn defines all question data.\n@SET(Q1, \"Q1_Response|Select one of the following options:|Option A|Option B|Option C\")@\n@SET(Q2, \"Q2_Response|Select all choices that apply:|Choice X|Choice Y|Choice Z\")@\n@SET(Q3, \"Q3_Response|Please select one from the dropdown list:|List Item 1|List Item 2|List Item 3\")@\n@SET(Q4, \"Q4_Response|Please provide a short, one-line answer\")@\n@SET(Q5, \"Q5_Response|Please provide a detailed answer in your own words:\")@\n@SET(Q6, \"Q6_Response|Select an option below, or provide your own answer.|Standard Answer 1|Standard Answer 2|Provide a custom answer:\")@",

            "show": false

        },

        {

            "user": "/ Turn 2: RADIO control\n@RADIO(@Q1[1]@, \"@Q1[2]@\", \"@Q1[3:5]@\")@",

            "show": true

        },

        {

            "user": "/ Turn 3: CHECKBOX control\n@CHECKBOX(@Q2[1]@, \"@Q2[2]@\", \"@Q2[3:5]@\")@",

            "show": true

        },

        {

            "user": "/ Turn 4: SELECT control\n@SELECT(@Q3[1]@, \"@Q3[2]@\", \"@Q3[3:5]@\")@",

            "show": true

        },

        {

            "user": "/ Turn 5: TEXT control\n@TEXT(@Q4[1]@, \"@Q4[2]@\")@",

            "show": true

        },

        {

            "user": "/ Turn 6: TEXTAREA control\n@TEXTAREA(@Q5[1]@, \"@Q5[2]@\")@",

            "show": true

        },

        {

            "user": "/ Turn 7: RADIO-Extended control\n@RADIO(@Q6[1]@, \"@Q6[2]@\", \"@Q6[3:4]@\", \"@Q6[5]@\")@",

            "show": true

        },

        {

            "system": "You are an expert analyst. Your task is to review the following questions, the available options, and the user's final responses. Provide a concise summary and analysis of the user's input.",

            "user": "Please analyze the following questionnaire responses:\n\n**Question 1:** @Q1[2]@\nResponse: @RADIO(@Q1[1]@)@\n\n**Question 2:** @Q2[2]@\nResponse: @CHECKBOX(@Q2[1]@)@\n\n**Question 3:** @Q3[2]@\nResponse: @SELECT(@Q3[1]@)@\n\n**Question 4:** @Q4[2]@\nResponse: @TEXT(@Q4[1]@)@\n\n**Question 5:** @Q5[2]@\nResponse: @TEXTAREA(@Q5[1]@)@\n\n**Question 6:** @Q6[2]@\nResponse: @RADIO(@Q6[1]@)@",

            "temperature": "0.1",

            "max-tokens": "5000",

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano"

        }

    ]

}

  

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params)

- Q1–Q6:  
    Each parameter is a self-contained survey unit storing:
    

- Response variable name
    
- Prompt text
    
- Valid options (if applicable)
    

This design centralizes survey definition and allows dynamic UI rendering via indexing.

### Execution Flow (prompts array)

- Turn 1 (Symbolic – Setup):  
    Uses @SET to define all survey questions and options in advance.
    
- Turns 2–7 (Symbolic – Survey Instrument):  
    Each turn presents a different input control:
    

- RADIO (single choice)
    
- CHECKBOX (multi-select)
    
- SELECT (dropdown)
    
- TEXT (short response)
    
- TEXTAREA (long response)
    
- RADIO-Extended (choice + custom input)
    

- Turn 8 (LLM – Simultaneous Investigator):  
    Receives all collected responses at once and produces a unified analytical summary.

# Real-time Job Satisfaction Survey Analytics: ASSISI-Based HR Feedback & Instant Insight

## Metadata

- Framework: ASSISI (AI-Supported Survey Instrument & Simultaneous Investigator)
    
- Domain: Human Resources / Organizational Analytics
    
- Complexity: Intermediate
    
- Primary Function: Employee Survey & Immediate Expert Analysis
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: SET, RADIO, CHECKBOX, SELECT, TEXTAREA
    
- Key Pattern: Structured Survey → Single-Pass LLM Synthesis
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Addressed  
    Traditional employee surveys often separate data collection from analysis, delaying insight and reducing responsiveness to workforce sentiment.
    
- Objective  
    This agent demonstrates how the ASSISI framework enables real-time HR analytics by collecting structured employee feedback and immediately synthesizing it into an actionable expert summary.
    
- Core Design Principle  
    All employee inputs are captured using symbolic UI controls first. Only after the full dataset is complete is it passed into a single LLM turn for holistic, context-aware analysis.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{

    "options": {

        "title": "Job Satisfaction Survey",

        "brief": "An interactive survey to gather employee feedback on job satisfaction, with real-time AI analysis.",

        "name": "ASSISI Example: Job Satisfaction Survey",

        "description": "This CAFA agent uses the ASSISI framework to conduct a multi-part job satisfaction survey, collecting data and then providing an instant, AI-driven summary of the employee's feedback.",

        "params": {}

        {

(Select all that apply)|Work-Life Balance|Company Culture|Compensation & Benefits|Challenging Projects|Team Collaboration\")@\n@SET(Q3, \"recommend_likelihood|How likely are you to recommend our company as a great place to work?|Very Likely|Likely|Neutral|Unlikely|Very Unlikely\")@\n@SET(Q4, \"improvement_areas|What is one thing we could do to improve your job satisfaction?|Please provide your suggestions here.\")@",

            "show": false

        },

        {

            "user": "/ Display Q1\n@RADIO(@Q1[1]@, \"@Q1[2]@\", \"@Q1[3:7]@\")@",

            "show": true

        },

        {

            "user": "/ Display Q2\n@CHECKBOX(@Q2[1]@, \"@Q2[2]@\", \"@Q2[3:7]@\")@",

            "show": true

        },

        {

            "user": "/ Display Q3\n@SELECT(@Q3[1]@, \"@Q3[2]@\", \"@Q3[3:7]@\")@",

            "show": true

        },

        {

            "user": "/ Display Q4\n@TEXTAREA(@Q4[1]@, \"@Q4[2]@\")@",

            "show": true

            "user": "Please analyze the following employee job satisfaction feedback:\n\n**1. Overall Satisfaction:**\n- Question: @Q1[2]@\n- Response: @RADIO(@Q1[1]@)@\n\n**2. Enjoyable Job Aspects:**\n- Question: @Q2[2]@\n- Response: @CHECKBOX(@Q2[1]@)@\n\n**3. Recommendation Likelihood:**\n- Question: @Q3[2]@\n- Response: @SELECT(@Q3[1]@)@\n\n**4. Areas for Improvement:**\n- Question: @Q4[2]@\n- Response: @TEXTAREA(@Q4[1]@)@",

            "temperature": "0.1",

            "max-tokens": "2000",

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano"

        }

    ]

}

  

## Execution Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (Implicit via SET)

- Q1–Q4  
    Each question parameter encapsulates:
    

- Response variable name
    
- Prompt text
    
- Valid options or text instruction
    

This creates a clean, maintainable survey definition layer.

### Survey Instrument Phase (Symbolic Turns)

- Turn 1 initializes all survey content invisibly
    
- Turns 2–5 present structured UI controls:
    

- RADIO → satisfaction score
    
- CHECKBOX → positive job aspects
    
- SELECT → recommendation likelihood
    
- TEXTAREA → qualitative improvement feedback
    

Each turn pauses execution until valid user input is received.

### Simultaneous Investigator Phase (LLM Turn)

- Final Turn receives all structured responses simultaneously
    
- The LLM acts as an HR analyst, synthesizing:
    

- Overall sentiment
    
- Positive engagement indicators
    
- Actionable improvement signals
    

This ensures consistent, real-time insight without iterative AI calls.

- “Route high-risk responses to a follow-up support agent.”
    

### Comparative Frameworks

- ASSISI vs IMPACT for HR conversations
    
- ASSISI vs OMG for policy-based responses
    
- ASSISI + SCREAM for diagnostic workforce assessments

# Adaptive Rubric Grader with RISE Evaluation: Nested REPEAT Rubric Selection and 3x Moderated Scoring

## Metadata

- Framework: ASSISI + RISE (ASSISI-style structured input → RISE-style repeated evaluation per criterion)
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Assessment & Evaluation
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: TEXTAREA, CHECKBOX, SET, REPEAT, TN, INDEX
    
- Key Concepts: Nested Looping, Linked Parallel Lists, User-Defined Rubric Assembly, Multi-pass LLM Evaluation, Criterion-Level Aggregation
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Static rubrics force the same criteria on every submission and can produce unstable LLM scoring due to single-pass judgment.
    
- Core Mechanism: The agent lets the user select grading criteria (outer loop) and runs three independent LLM evaluations per selected criterion (inner repeated passes), then aggregates each criterion’s three reports and compiles a final multi-criterion summary.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{

    "options": {

        "title": "Nested-Loop Grader with 3x RISE Evaluation",

        "brief": "For each user-selected criterion, this agent performs a fixed 3-turn evaluation and compiles the results.",

        "name": "Nested RISE Grader TN Version",

        "description": "This advanced agent uses a nested loop structure. An outer REPEAT loop iterates through multiple user-selected criteria. For each criterion, a manual 3-turn inner loop provides a robust evaluation. The results are aggregated at each stage, providing a comprehensive final report.",

        "greeting": "Welcome to the Nested-Loop Grader. Please paste the essay you would like to grade.",

        "params": {

            "CRITERIA": {

                "org": "Clarity|Evidence|Structure|Originality",

                "cond": "SELF",

                "desc": "The master list of all possible grading criteria."

            },

            "RUBRICS": {

                "org": "You are a writing expert. Score the CLARITY of the essay from 1-10. Clarity refers to how easy the writing is to understand, the precision of the language, and the absence of ambiguity. Provide a score and a 1-2 sentence justification for this iteration.|You are an academic reviewer. Score the use of EVIDENCE from 1-10. Evidence refers to the quality, relevance, and integration of supporting facts, data, or quotes used to substantiate the argument. Provide a score and a 1-2 sentence justification for this iteration.|You are a structural editor. Score the STRUCTURE of the essay from 1-10. Structure refers to the logical flow of the argument, including the introduction, thesis, body paragraphs, and conclusion. Provide a score and a 1-2 sentence justification for this iteration.|You are a creative thinking analyst. Score the ORIGINALITY of the essay from 1-10. Originality refers to the novelty of the ideas, the uniqueness of the perspective, or the creativity of the approach to the topic. Provide a score and a 1-2 sentence justification for this iteration.",

                "cond": "LINK(CRITERIA)",

                "desc": "The parallel list of detailed rubrics, linked to the CRITERIA list."

            }

        }

    },

    "prompts": [

        {

            "user": "/ This turn captures the user's essay.\n@TEXTAREA(\"essay_text\", \"Please paste the essay here:\")@",

            "show": true

        },

            "user": "/ This turn asks the user to select the criteria to apply.\n@CHECKBOX(\"selected_criteria\", \"Please select all the criteria for which you want a 3x evaluation:\", \"@CRITERIA@\")@",

        },

        },

            "show": false

        },

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano",

            "temperature": "0.1",

            "max-tokens": "2000"

        },

        {

            "system": "@RUBRICS[@RUBRIC_INDEX@]@",

            "user": "This is grading iteration #2 for the criterion '@CURRENT_CRITERION[@R_i@]@'. Please grade the following essay.\n\n---\n\n@TEXTAREA(essay_text)@",

            "show": false,

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano",

            "temperature": "0.1",

            "max-tokens": "2000"

        },

        {

            "system": "@RUBRICS[@RUBRIC_INDEX@]@",

            "user": "This is grading iteration #3 for the criterion '@CURRENT_CRITERION[@R_i@]@'. Please grade the following essay.\n\n---\n\n@TEXTAREA(essay_text)@",

            "show": false,

            "show": true,

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano",

            "markdown": true,

            "temperature": "0.1",

            "max-tokens": "2000"

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- CRITERIA: Pipe-separated master list used to populate the CHECKBOX input. cond: SELF preserves authored ordering.
    
- RUBRICS: Parallel list of rubric prompts. cond: LINK(CRITERIA) ensures each rubric remains aligned with its matching criterion name.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic): Essay capture via @TEXTAREA("essay_text", ...)@.
    
- Turn 2 (Symbolic): User selects evaluation criteria via @CHECKBOX("selected_criteria", ..., "@CRITERIA@")@.
    
- Turn 3 (Symbolic, Hidden): Stores selections into USER_CHOICES with @SET.
    
- Turn 4 (Symbolic, Hidden): Outer loop controller using @REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(5)@, @USER_CHOICES[N]@)@ to run Turns 5–9 once per selected criterion.
    
- Turn 5 (Symbolic, Hidden, Outer Loop Body): Sets the current criterion and computes its rubric index via @INDEX("@CRITERIA@", "@CURRENT_CRITERION@")@.
    
- Turn 6 (LLM, Hidden): Grading iteration 1 using rubric prompt @RUBRICS[@RUBRIC_INDEX@]@.
    
- Turn 7 (LLM, Hidden): Grading iteration 2 using the same rubric prompt.
    
- Turn 8 (LLM, Hidden): Grading iteration 3 using the same rubric prompt.
    
- Turn 9 (LLM, Hidden): Aggregates the three iteration reports for the current criterion using loop-scoped turn references: @TR@TN(-3)@[@R_i@]@, @TR@TN(-2)@[@R_i@]@, @TR@TN(-1)@[@R_i@]@.
    
- Turn 10 (LLM, Visible): Compiles all criterion-level aggregated reports (concatenated from Turn 9 across outer-loop iterations) into a final student-facing summary using @TR@TN(-1)@@.

    B --> C(T2: Select Criteria CHECKBOX)

    C --> D(T3: Store USER_CHOICES SET - Hidden)

    D --> E{T4: Outer REPEAT over USER_CHOICES - Hidden}

    E --> F(T5: Set CURRENT_CRITERION + RUBRIC_INDEX - Hidden)

    F --> G(T6: Grade Iteration 1 - LLM Hidden)

    G --> H(T7: Grade Iteration 2 - LLM Hidden)

    H --> I(T8: Grade Iteration 3 - LLM Hidden)

    I --> J(T9: Aggregate 3 Reports - LLM Hidden)

    J --> E

    E -->|Loop complete| K(T10: Final Compilation - LLM Visible)

    K --> L[End]

# Dynamic Task Assistant: AJOTA + STAR Framework

## Metadata

- Framework: AJOTA + STAR
    
- Complexity: Intermediate
    
- Primary Function: Personalized Task Assistant
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: TEXT, RADIO, SET, INDEX
    
- Key LLM Features: Task mining, prompt generation, just-in-time guidance
    

## Background & Objective

This agent extends the STAR (Single-Turn Agent Replicator) pattern by adding AJOTA (AI-based Job and Task Analysis) as a dynamic setup phase.

- AJOTA Phase: Collect job title → generate task list → generate matching system prompts → store both as Agent Parameters.
    
- STAR Phase: User selects a task → agent loads the corresponding system prompt → executes the task in a single-turn assistant mode.
    

This shifts the agent from a fixed-purpose tool to a self-configuring assistant that adapts to many professions without hardcoding domain logic.

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### AJOTA Phase (Turns 1–6)

- Turn 1 (Symbolic): Captures the job title using TEXT.
    
- Turn 2 (LLM, Hidden): Generates a pipe-separated list of tasks for that job.
    
- Turn 3 (LLM, Hidden): Generates a pipe-separated list of system prompts aligned to the task list order.
    
- Turn 4 (Symbolic, Hidden): Stores both lists into Agent Parameters TASK_AP and SYSTEM_PROMPT_AP.
    
- Turn 5 (Symbolic): Displays TASK_AP as a RADIO menu for user selection.
    
- Turn 6 (Symbolic, Hidden): Uses @INDEX to compute TASK_INDEX, the lookup key into SYSTEM_PROMPT_AP.
    

### STAR Phase (Turns 7–10)

- Turn 7 (LLM, Hidden): Produces a short “how to ask” guide for the selected task.
    
- Turn 8 (Symbolic, Hidden): Saves the guide as GUIDE_TEXT_AP.
    
- Turn 9 (Symbolic): Displays the guide text.
    
- Turn 10 (LLM, Visible): Loads the task-specific system prompt @SYSTEM_PROMPT_AP[@TASK_INDEX@]@, waits for user input, and executes the chosen task as a single-turn specialist.

# AIG² TAP: Generating Items by Permuting Task Features

## Metadata

- Framework: AIG² TAP IOTA
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Automatic Item Generation (AIG) via feature permutation
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: TEXT, CHECKBOX, SET, REPEAT, JUMP, MAP, EVAL
    
- Key Design Pattern: Simulated nested loop (outer loop via JUMP+MAP, inner loop via REPEAT)
    
- Output Type: Polished quiz report (Organizer LLM turn)
    

## Background & Objective

Automatic Item Generation (AIG) aims to create many assessment items systematically, by permuting deep item features (e.g., cognitive level, item format) to control item focus and difficulty. In traditional programming this usually requires nested loops (“for each cognitive level, for each item format…”).

CAFA does not provide a native nested-loop command, so this agent demonstrates a practical workaround:

- Outer Loop (manual loop): uses JUMP + MAP + EVAL to repeatedly return to the outer-loop “start” until all cognitive levels are processed.
    
- Inner Loop (standard loop): uses REPEAT to iterate through all selected item formats for the current cognitive level.
    
- Quality finish: a final “Organizer” LLM turn converts the raw concatenated output into a clean, labeled quiz report.
    

The user configures the quiz by providing:

1. a domain/topic, 2) cognitive levels, 3) item formats, and 4) number of items per feature-combination.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

        "title": "Custom Quiz Generator",

Provide only the generated quiz items themselves, clearly numbered if more than one, without any extra conversation.",

For each item, clearly label its cognitive level and format. You will be told how many items were generated for each combination; ensure your final report accounts for all of them. Conclude the report with a simple closing statement.",

            "show": false

            "user": "/ T12: Check if the outer loop should continue. If so, jump back to T6.\n@JUMP(@MAP(\"@EVAL(\"@LEVEL_INDEX@ <= @USER_LEVELS[N]@\")@\", \"true\", \"6|@TN(1)@\")@)@",

            "show": false

The original request was for the domain '@USER_DOMAIN@' with these levels: '@USER_LEVELS@' and these formats: '@USER_FORMATS@'. Crucially, @USER_NUM_ITEMS@ items were generated for each combination.\n\n**Raw Data Pile:**\n@GENERATED_ITEMS@",

            "show": true,

            "markdown": true,

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano"

        }

    ]

}

  

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Phase 1: User Input & Initialization (T1–T5)

- T1–T4 (Symbolic): Collect domain, cognitive levels, item formats, and items-per-combination.
    
- T5 (Symbolic, Hidden): Stores inputs as stable parameters and initializes:
    

- LEVEL_INDEX = 1 (outer-loop counter)
    
- GENERATED_ITEMS = "" (final accumulator)
    

### Phase 2: Simulated Nested Loop (T6–T12)

Outer loop entry point:

- T6 (Visible): Announces current cognitive level using @USER_LEVELS[@LEVEL_INDEX@]@.
    

Inner loop:

- T7 (Hidden): @REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(1)@, @USER_FORMATS[N]@)@ repeats only T8 once per selected format.
    
- T8 (LLM): Generates USER_NUM_ITEMS items for the current:
    

- Domain (USER_DOMAIN)
    
- Cognitive Level (USER_LEVELS[LEVEL_INDEX])
    
- Item Format (USER_FORMATS[@R_i@]) — note: here @R_i@ refers to the inner-loop counter.
    

Data integrity fix:

- T9 (Hidden): Captures the entire concatenated inner-loop output into TEMP_RESULTS. This prevents loss/overwrite when the outer loop iterates again.
    

Outer loop continuation:

- T11 (Hidden): Appends TEMP_RESULTS into GENERATED_ITEMS and increments LEVEL_INDEX.
    
- T12 (Hidden): Checks whether more levels remain:
    

- If yes → JUMP back to T6
    
- If no → falls through to the Organizer (T13)
    

### Phase 3: Final Report (T13)

- T13 (LLM, Visible): Organizes GENERATED_ITEMS into a clean quiz document, labeling items by cognitive level + format and ensuring the expected counts per combination.
    

## Mermaid Diagram

graph TD

    A[T1–T4: Collect Inputs ⚙️] --> B[T5: Initialize Variables ⚙️]

    B --> C[T6: Outer Loop Start Announcement ⚙️]

    C --> D[T7: Inner Loop REPEAT Setup ⚙️]

    D --> E[T8: Generate Items (LLM) 🤖]

    D -->|after repeats| F[T9: Capture Inner Results ⚙️]

    F --> G[T10: Inner Loop Complete Notice ⚙️]

    G --> H[T11: Append + LEVEL_INDEX++ ⚙️]

    H --> I{T12: More Levels? ⚙️}

    I -->|Yes| C

    I -->|No| J[T13: Organizer (LLM) 🤖]

- “Modify this agent so the outer loop is also REPEAT-based (no manual JUMP), using a precomputed list of (level, format) pairs.”
    
- “Add Structured Output to T8 so each generated item follows a strict schema (Stem|Options|Answer|Rationale).”
    
- “Generate distractor rationales automatically for multiple-choice items and ensure each distractor maps to a misconception tag.”
    
- “Add a post-processing turn that produces a teacher-friendly answer key with scoring guidance.”
    
- “Save the final quiz using SAVE(LOG) and provide a retrieval ID so it can be reused later.”
