# Dynamic Matching & Hybrid Grading with OMEGA: Dynamic Ontology + 5-Round 4x4 Matching with LLM Short-Answer Scoring

## Metadata

- Framework: IOTA, OMEGA
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Assessment (Hybrid: Symbolic + LLM Grading)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: TEXTAREA, SET, SHUFFLE, LINK, REPEAT, EVAL, RADIO, SORT, D, MAP, TEXT, TR, TN
    
- Key Concepts: OMEGA (LLM-emulated ontology), Testlet slicing via index math, Distractor permutation pools, Dual-mode assessment (recognition vs recall), Ground-truth-anchored LLM grading
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Matching assessments are difficult to author at quality (permutations/distractors) and difficult to grade when answers are free-text and format-flexible.
    
- Core Mechanism: Generates a 20-item ontology from a user topic via LLM (terms + stems), shuffles while preserving linkage, then runs a 5-round loop that builds 4x4 matching items with shuffled options and distractor permutations, grading once deterministically (RADIO+MAP) and once flexibly (TEXT+LLM grader anchored by the symbolic correct key).
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{  

    "options": {  

        "title": "OMEGA: Dynamic Matching & Short Answer Quiz",  

        "brief": "A multi-round quiz with dynamic content, 4x4 matching, and LLM-graded short answers.",  

        "name": "OMEGA Dynamic Matching + SA Quiz",  

        "description": "This agent uses the OMEGA framework. It asks for a topic, generates a 20-item ontology (questions/answers), and then administers a 5-round quiz. Each round includes one 4x4 matching item and one LLM-graded short answer question reusing one of the matching stems.",  

        "greeting": "Welcome! I can generate a custom matching and short answer quiz on any topic. Please provide the assessment context to begin.",  

        "keep-in-app-cafakey": false,  

        "is-template": false,  

        "is-public": false,  

        "params": {  

            "KEYTERM_PERSONA": {  

                "org": "You are an expert knowledge extractor. Based on the provided topic, generate exactly 20 key terms or keywords. Your response MUST be ONLY a single pipe-separated list of these 20 terms.",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "System prompt for T2 to generate 20 answer terms."  

            },  

            "STEM_PERSONA": {  

                "org": "You are an expert assessment designer. You will be given a pipe-separated list of 20 terms. For each term, generate a short, clear definition or question (stem). Your response MUST be ONLY a single pipe-separated list of these 20 stems, in the exact same order as the terms.",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "System prompt for T3 to generate 20 question stems."  

            },  

            "GRADER_PERSONA": {  

                "org": "You are an expert grader. You will be given a question, the user's free-text answer, and the correct answer. Compare the user's answer to the correct answer. Respond with 'Correct' or 'Incorrect' followed by a brief, one-sentence explanation of why.",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "System prompt for the LLM-based short answer grader."  

            },  

            "Qs": {  

                "org": "temp",  

                "cond": "SHUFFLE",  

                "desc": "Dynamically populated with 20 generated questions."  

            },  

            "As": {  

                "org": "temp",  

                "cond": "LINK(Qs)",  

                "desc": "Dynamically populated with 20 generated answers, linked to Qs."  

            }  

        }  

    },  

    "prompts": [  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T1: Ask the user for the assessment context.\n@TEXTAREA(\"assessment_context\", \"What topic or context should this 20-item quiz cover (e.g., 'Introductory Statistics', 'The Solar System')?\")@",  

            "show": true,  

            "markdown": true,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "@KEYTERM_PERSONA@",  

            "user": "Context: @TEXTAREA(assessment_context)@",  

            "temperature": "0.1",  

            "max-tokens": "2000",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano",  

            "output-values": "A1|A2|A3|A4|A5|A6|A7|A8|A9|A10|A11|A12|A13|A14|A15|A16|A17|A18|A19|A20"  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "@STEM_PERSONA@",  

            "user": "Terms: @TR@TN(-1)@@",  

            "temperature": "0.1",  

            "max-tokens": "4000",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano",  

            "output-values": "Q1|Q2|Q3|Q4|Q5|Q6|Q7|Q8|Q9|Q10|Q11|Q12|Q13|Q14|Q15|Q16|Q17|Q18|A19|Q20"  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T4: Store the dynamically generated ontology. Qs (Stems) from T3, As (Terms) from T2.\n@SET(Qs, \"@TR@TN(-1)@@\", \"SHUFFLE\")@\n@SET(As, \"@TR@TN(-2)@@\", \"LINK(Qs)\")@",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T5: Setup a 5-round REPEAT loop to run T6-T13 (8 turns) five times.\n@REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(8)@, 5)@",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T6 (Loop T1/8): Create a 4-item testlet (STEMS, ANS) for this round.\n@SET(STEMS, \"@Qs[@EVAL(\"(@R_i@-1)*4+1\")@:@EVAL(\"(@R_i@-1)*4+4\")@]@\", \"SELF\")@\n@SET(ANS, \"@As[@EVAL(\"(@R_i@-1)*4+1\")@:@EVAL(\"(@R_i@-1)*4+4\")@]@\", \"LINK(STEMS)\")@",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T7 (Loop T2/8): Create the 4-item shuffled answer list (ANSS4) and its linked key (MAI).\n@SET(ANSS4, \"@ANS[1:4]@\", \"SHUFFLE\")@\n@SET(MAI, \"a|b|c|d\", \"LINK(ANSS4)\")@",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T8 (Loop T3/8): Create the 23 incorrect permutations (distractors).\n@SET(DISTRACTORS, \"@MAI[1]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[4]@, @MAI[3]@|@MAI[1]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[4]@|@MAI[1]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[4]@, @MAI[2]@|@MAI[1]@, @MAI[4]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[3]@|@MAI[1]@, @MAI[4]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[2]@|@MAI[2]@, @MAI[1]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[4]@|@MAI[2]@, @MAI[1]@, @MAI[4]@, @MAI[3]@|@MAI[2]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[1]@, @MAI[4]@|@MAI[2]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[4]@, @MAI[1]@|@MAI[2]@, @MAI[4]@, @MAI[1]@, @MAI[3]@|@MAI[2]@, @MAI[4]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[1]@|@MAI[3]@, @MAI[1]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[4]@|@MAI[3]@, @MAI[1]@, @MAI[4]@, @MAI[2]@|@MAI[3]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[1]@, @MAI[4]@|@MAI[3]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[4]@, @MAI[1]@|@MAI[3]@, @MAI[4]@, @MAI[1]@, @MAI[2]@|@MAI[3]@, @MAI[4]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[1]@|@MAI[4]@, @MAI[1]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[3]@|@MAI[4]@, @MAI[1]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[2]@|@MAI[4]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[1]@, @MAI[3]@|@MAI[4]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[1]@|@MAI[4]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[1]@, @MAI[2]@|@MAI[4]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[1]@ \", \"SHUFFLE\")@",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T9 (Loop T4/8): Display the 4x4 matching question with 10 shuffled options.\n@RADIO(\n\"MA\", \n\"Match the information in Premises column with the information in Responses column.\n\n| Premises | Responses |\n| :--- | :--- |\n| a. @STEMS[1]@ | @ANSS4[1]@ |\n| b. @STEMS[2]@ | @ANSS4[2]@ |\n| c. @STEMS[3]@ | @ANSS4[3]@ |\n| d. @STEMS[4]@ | @ANSS4[4]@\n <br>\",\n\"@SORT(\"@D(\"@MAI[1]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[4]@\", \"\", \"@DISTRACTORS[1:9]@\", \"10\")@\")@\"\n)@",  

            "markdown": true,  

            "show": true,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T10 (Loop T5/8): Grade the matching selection using MAP (Symbolic) and show the result.\n@MAP(\"@RADIO(MA)@\", \"@MAI[1]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[4]@\", \"correct|wrong\")@",  

            "show": true,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T11 (Loop T6/8): Ask the *same* 4x4 matching question as a short answer (TEXT) input.\n@TEXT(\"sa_@R_i@\", \"Short Answer: Match the items. Provide your answer as comma-separated labels (e.g., a, b, c, d).\n\n| Premises | Responses |\n| :--- | :--- |\n| a. @STEMS[1]@ | @ANSS4[1]@ |\n| b. @STEMS[2]@ | @ANSS4[2]@ |\n| c. @STEMS[3]@ | @ANSS4[3]@ |\n| d. @STEMS[4]@ | @ANSS4[4]@\n <br>\")@",  

            "markdown": true,  

            "show": true,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "@GRADER_PERSONA@",  

            "user": "/ T12 (Loop T7/8): Grade the short answer using an LLM.\n**Short Answer Grade:**\n\n- Question: \nMatch the information in Premises column with the information in Responses column. Answer should be comma-separated Premises labels, for example, a, b, c, d.\n\n| Premises | Responses |\n| :--- | :--- |\n| a. @STEMS[1]@ | @ANSS4[1]@ |\n| b. @STEMS[2]@ | @ANSS4[2]@ |\n| c. @STEMS[3]@ | @ANSS4[3]@ |\n| d. @STEMS[4]@ | @ANSS4[4]@\n\n- Correct Answer: @MAI[1]@, @MAI[2]@, @MAI[3]@, @MAI[4]@\n- User's Answer: @TEXT(sa_@R_i@)@",  

            "temperature": "0.1",  

            "max-tokens": "2000",  

            "markdown": true,  

            "show": true,  

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano"  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T13 (Loop T8/8): This is an empty placeholder turn to correctly define the loop block. It will be skipped.\n",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T14: Display completion message after all rounds are finished.\nQuiz Complete! You have finished all 5 rounds.",  

            "show": true,  

            "model": null  

        }  

    ]  

}

  

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- KEYTERM_PERSONA: LLM system prompt used to generate exactly 20 key terms (answers) from the user topic.
    
- STEM_PERSONA: LLM system prompt used to generate 20 stems/definitions in the exact same order as the 20 terms.
    
- GRADER_PERSONA: LLM system prompt used to grade the short-answer permutation using provided ground truth.
    
- Qs: Dynamic stem list storage; cond: SHUFFLE enables randomized ordering after generation.
    
- As: Dynamic answer list storage; cond: LINK(Qs) preserves correct term↔stem pairing after Qs shuffles.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic UI): Topic intake via @TEXTAREA(assessment_context, ...)@.
    
- Turn 2 (LLM Hidden): Generates 20 key terms (pipe-separated) using KEYTERM_PERSONA; constrained by output-values.
    
- Turn 3 (LLM Hidden): Generates 20 stems (pipe-separated) using STEM_PERSONA based on Turn 2 output.
    
- Turn 4 (Symbolic): Stores ontology: SET(Qs, T3, SHUFFLE) then SET(As, T2, LINK(Qs)).
    
- Turn 5 (Symbolic): Starts a 5-iteration loop: @REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(8)@, 5)@ executing Turns 6–13 each round.
    
- Turn 6 (Symbolic, Loop): Builds the round’s 4-item testlet (STEMS/ANS) by slicing Qs/As with EVAL index math derived from @R_i@.
    
- Turn 7 (Symbolic, Loop): Shuffles the 4 answers into ANSS4 and creates the linked correct key MAI (a|b|c|d LINKed to ANSS4).
    
- Turn 8 (Symbolic, Loop): Precomputes 23 incorrect permutations and shuffles them into DISTRACTORS.
    
- Turn 9 (Symbolic UI, Loop): Presents 4x4 matching grid and a RADIO choice list of 10 options (1 correct + 9 distractors), shuffled for display.
    
- Turn 10 (Symbolic UI, Loop): Deterministic grading of RADIO selection via @MAP(@RADIO(MA)@, correct_string, "correct|wrong")@.
    
- Turn 11 (Symbolic UI, Loop): Re-asks the same matching grid as free-text via @TEXT(sa_@R_i@, ...)@.
    
- Turn 12 (LLM Visible, Loop): Hybrid grading: GRADER_PERSONA compares the user’s free-text answer to the symbolically preserved correct answer (MAI[1..4]) and outputs Correct/Incorrect + explanation.
    
- Turn 13 (Symbolic Hidden, Loop): Empty placeholder to define loop block end (skipped).
    
- Turn 14 (Symbolic UI): Post-loop completion message.
    

## Visualization Mermaid Code

graph TD

  A[Start] --> B[Turn 1: TEXTAREA Topic Input]

  B --> C[Turn 2: LLM Generate 20 Terms (KEYTERM_PERSONA)]

  C --> D[Turn 3: LLM Generate 20 Stems (STEM_PERSONA)]

  D --> E[Turn 4: SET Qs=Stems (SHUFFLE) + SET As=Terms (LINK Qs)]

  E --> F{Turn 5: REPEAT 5 Rounds<br/>Loop Turns 6-13}

  

  F --> G[Turn 6: Slice 4-item Testlet (STEMS/ANS) via EVAL + LINK]

  G --> H[Turn 7: SHUFFLE ANS->ANSS4 + LINK MAI to ANSS4]

  H --> I[Turn 8: Build + SHUFFLE 23 Permutation DISTRACTORS]

  I --> J[Turn 9: RADIO Matching (10 options = 1 correct + 9 distractors)]

  J --> K[Turn 10: Symbolic Grade via MAP(RADIO vs correct MAI)]

  K --> L[Turn 11: TEXT Short Answer (same grid)]

  L --> M[Turn 12: LLM Grade vs Ground Truth (MAI)]

  M --> N[Turn 13: Placeholder (skipped)]

  N --> F

  

  F -->|after 5 rounds| O[Turn 14: Quiz Complete Message]

  O --> P[End]

  

## Related Questions and Instructions

### Design & Architecture Requests

- Framework Related:  
    “Generate a MACRO agent that uses OMEGA-style dynamic ontology generation (LLM → SET/SHUFFLE/LINK) before assessment.”
    
- Structure Related:  
    “Create a REPEAT-based multi-round matching quiz that includes both RADIO and TEXT versions of the same item.”
    
- Complexity Related:  
    “Generate an advanced hybrid-grading assessment agent that anchors the LLM grader with a symbolic ground truth key.”
    

### Usage & Modification Requests

- Task Related:  
    “Swap matching (a–d) to a 5x5 format while keeping the same two-stage grading pattern.”
    
- Reuse:  
    “Reuse this structure for language learning (vocabulary ↔ definitions) with 20 generated pairs.”
    
- Bounded Changes:  
    “Change only the number of rounds (5 → 3) without adding new turns.”
    

Modification Recipes (If/Then):

- To Add Numeric Scoring: If you need a running score, then insert a hidden @SET(USER_SCORE, "0")@ immediately after Turn 4, and insert a hidden scoring update immediately after Turn 10 using @MAP(...)@ to convert correct/wrong to 1|0, then add the increment with @EVAL(...)@.
    
- To Require Machine-Parseable LLM Grades: If you need symbolic post-processing of Turn 12, then modify GRADER_PERSONA so the first token is strictly Correct or Incorrect (unchanged otherwise), and add a hidden turn after Turn 12 that maps that first token to 1|0.
    
- To Add OMEGA Generation Validation: If you need guardrails before the quiz loop, then insert a hidden symbolic validation turn between Turn 3 and Turn 4 that checks list integrity (e.g., expected count) and uses @JUMP() to route to an error message turn if invalid.
    
- To Add AGILE Logging: If you need to persist results, then add a final hidden turn after Turn 14 that compiles per-round data into a single string parameter and calls @SAVE(..., "LOG", "true")@.
    

## References

- Choi, J. (2025). Dynamic Matching & Hybrid Grading with OMEGA: Dynamic Ontology + 5-Round 4x4 Matching with LLM Short-Answer Scoring. In Collective AI on the Foundation AI (CAFA): The pathway of digital transformation of intelligence. CAFA Lab, Inc.

# JSON-based Quiz System using FISH Framework: JP Quiz Bank with Symbolic Topic Routing

## Metadata

- Framework: FISH, IOTA
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Assessment (Deterministic Quiz Delivery + Symbolic Grading)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: RADIO, SET, INDEX, SETJ, REPEAT, MAP
    
- Key Concepts: FISH (Filing + Intelligent Search Hybrid), JSON Parameter (JP) ontology, Dynamic property access, Loop-based quiz administration, Order-stable topic→key routing via LINK
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: LLM-based quiz generation can hallucinate answers; maintaining multiple quizzes as scattered parameters is hard to scale and audit.
    
- Core Mechanism: Stores multiple quizzes inside one JP (QUIZ_BANK), lets the user pick a topic via RADIO, symbolically maps the UI choice to an internal JSON key, retrieves the selected quiz array into CURRENT_QUIZ via SETJ, then administers and grades questions deterministically inside a REPEAT loop.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{  

    "options": {  

        "title": "FISH Framework: JP-Based Quiz System",  

        "name": "FISH Framework (Symbolic JP) Quiz",  

        "brief": "A quiz agent that uses FISH to retrieve one of three quizzes from a master JSON Parameter.",  

        "description": "This agent uses FISH Approach 3. A master JP (QUIZ_BANK) holds three quizzes. A RADIO button (Symbolic Search) lets the user pick one. The agent retrieves the selected quiz data using dynamic property access (@QUIZ_BANK.@SELECTED_KEY@), stores it in CURRENT_QUIZ, and administers the 2-question quiz.",  

        "greeting": "Welcome to the quiz system! Please select a topic to begin.",  

        "params": {  

            "QUIZ_TOPICS": {  

                "org": "Statistics|History|Science",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "The user-facing list of quiz topics for the RADIO control."  

            },  

            "QUIZ_KEYS": {  

                "org": "quiz_stats|quiz_history|quiz_science",  

                "cond": "LINK(QUIZ_TOPICS)",  

                "desc": "The internal JSON keys for each quiz, LINKED to QUIZ_TOPICS."  

            },  

            "QUIZ_BANK": {  

                "org": "{\"quiz_stats\":[{\"stem\":\"What is the mean of 2, 4, and 6?\",\"options\":\"2|3|4|5\",\"answer\":\"4\"},{\"stem\":\"What is the median of 1, 2, and 5?\",\"options\":\"1|2|5|3\",\"answer\":\"2\"}],\"quiz_history\":[{\"stem\":\"In what year did World War II end?\",\"options\":\"1940|1945|1950|1955\",\"answer\":\"1945\"},{\"stem\":\"Who was the first President of the United States?\",\"options\":\"Adams|Jefferson|Washington|Hamilton\",\"answer\":\"Washington\"}],\"quiz_science\":[{\"stem\":\"What is the chemical symbol for Gold?\",\"options\":\"Go|Au|Ag|Gd\",\"answer\":\"Au\"},{\"stem\":\"What planet is known as the Red Planet?\",\"options\":\"Jupiter|Mars|Venus|Saturn\",\"answer\":\"Mars\"}]}"  

            },  

            "CURRENT_QUIZ": {  

                "org": "[]"  

            },  

            "SELECTED_KEY": {  

                "org": "",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "An AP to store the JSON key for the selected quiz."  

            },  

            "TOTAL_QUESTIONS": {  

                "org": "2",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "The number of questions in each quiz."  

            }  

        }  

    },  

    "prompts": [  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T1: 'Intelligent Search' (Symbolic). Ask user to select a quiz topic.\n@RADIO(\"topic_choice\", \"Please select a quiz topic:\", \"@QUIZ_TOPICS@\")@",  

            "show": true  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T2: Map the user's choice to the internal JSON key.\n@SET(KEY_INDEX, \"@INDEX(\"@QUIZ_TOPICS@\", \"@RADIO(topic_choice)@\")@\")@\n@SET(SELECTED_KEY, \"@QUIZ_KEYS[@KEY_INDEX@]@\")@",  

            "show": false  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T3: 'Filing/Retrieval' (FISH). Retrieve the selected quiz array from the master QUIZ_BANK JP.\n@SETJ(CURRENT_QUIZ, @QUIZ_BANK.@SELECTED_KEY@@)@",  

            "show": false  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T4: Setup the REPEAT loop to run for the number of questions.\n@REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(2)@, @TOTAL_QUESTIONS@)@",  

            "show": false  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T5 (LOOP 1/2): Ask the question for the current iteration.\n@RADIO(\"ans_@R_i@\", \"@CURRENT_QUIZ[@R_i@].stem@\", \"@CURRENT_QUIZ[@R_i@].options@\")@",  

            "show": true  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T6 (LOOP 2/2): Grade the question and store the result.\n@SET(RESULT_@R_i@, \"@MAP(\"@RADIO(ans_@R_i@)@\", \"@CURRENT_QUIZ[@R_i@].answer@\", \"Correct|Incorrect\")@\")@",  

            "show": false  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T7: Display the final summary.\n## Quiz Results for @RADIO(topic_choice)@\n\n**Question 1: @CURRENT_QUIZ[1].stem@**\n- Your Answer: @RADIO(ans_1)@\n- Correct Answer: @CURRENT_QUIZ[1].answer@\n- Result: @RESULT_1@\n\n**Question 2: @CURRENT_QUIZ[2].stem@**\n- Your Answer: @RADIO(ans_2)@\n- Correct Answer: @CURRENT_QUIZ[2].answer@\n- Result: @RESULT_2@",  

            "show": true,  

            "markdown": true  

        }  

    ]  

}

  

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- QUIZ_TOPICS: User-facing topic list used in RADIO(topic_choice) for symbolic selection UI.
    
- QUIZ_KEYS: Internal JSON key list aligned to QUIZ_TOPICS via LINK(QUIZ_TOPICS) (UI label → machine key mapping).
    
- QUIZ_BANK: Master JP “filing cabinet” JSON object holding multiple quizzes; each quiz key maps to a JSON array of question objects (stem, options, answer).
    
- CURRENT_QUIZ: Temporary JP state variable initialized to [], populated by SETJ with the selected quiz array.
    
- SELECTED_KEY: Temporary AP state variable holding the chosen quiz key string (e.g., quiz_history).
    
- TOTAL_QUESTIONS: Loop control AP specifying how many iterations REPEAT should run.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic, UI): Collects the user’s topic selection via @RADIO("topic_choice", ..., "@QUIZ_TOPICS@")@.
    
- Turn 2 (Symbolic): Bridges UI → data structure:
    

- INDEX(QUIZ_TOPICS, RADIO(topic_choice)) → KEY_INDEX
    
- QUIZ_KEYS[KEY_INDEX] → SELECTED_KEY
    

- Turn 3 (Symbolic): Retrieves the selected quiz from JP using dynamic property access and preserves JSON via @SETJ(CURRENT_QUIZ, @QUIZ_BANK.@SELECTED_KEY@@)@.
    
- Turn 4 (Symbolic): Starts loop over questions with @REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(2)@, @TOTAL_QUESTIONS@)@ (runs Turns 5–6).
    
- Turn 5 (Symbolic, UI, Loop): Asks the current question using JP indexing and field access:
    

- @CURRENT_QUIZ[@R_i@].stem@ and @CURRENT_QUIZ[@R_i@].options@
    

- Turn 6 (Symbolic, Loop): Deterministic grading and per-item storage using:
    

- MAP(user_choice, correct_answer, "Correct|Incorrect") → RESULT_@R_i@
    

- Turn 7 (Symbolic, UI): Post-loop report referencing CURRENT_QUIZ content, user answers, and stored RESULT_1/RESULT_2.

graph TD

  A[Start] --> B[Turn 1: RADIO topic_choice (QUIZ_TOPICS)]

  B --> C[Turn 2: INDEX selection -> KEY_INDEX<br/>SET SELECTED_KEY = QUIZ_KEYS[KEY_INDEX]]

  C --> D[Turn 3: SETJ CURRENT_QUIZ = QUIZ_BANK.SELECTED_KEY]

  D --> E[Turn 4: REPEAT over TOTAL_QUESTIONS (Turns 5-6)]

  E --> F[Turn 5 (Loop): RADIO ans_Ri<br/>stem/options from CURRENT_QUIZ[Ri]]

  F --> G[Turn 6 (Loop): SET RESULT_Ri = MAP(user_answer vs answer)]

  G --> E

  E --> H[Turn 7: Display Summary (Q1/Q2 + results)]

  H --> I[End]

  

## Related Questions and Instructions

### Design & Architecture Requests

- Framework Related:  
    “Generate a MACRO agent that follows FISH Approach 3 using a JSON Parameter as the filing cabinet.”
    
- Structure Related:  
    “Create a quiz selector that maps a RADIO UI choice to a JP key using INDEX + LINKed key lists.”
    
- Complexity Related:  
    “Generate an advanced symbolic assessment agent with JP retrieval and looped delivery.”
    

### Usage & Modification Requests

- Task Related:  
    “Add a new quiz topic by extending QUIZ_TOPICS/QUIZ_KEYS and adding a new key in QUIZ_BANK.”
    
- Reuse:  
    “Reuse this JP-based quiz bank pattern for onboarding compliance quizzes.”
    
- Bounded Changes:  
    “Change only the quiz length by adjusting TOTAL_QUESTIONS without adding turns.”
    

Modification Recipes (If/Then):

- To Support Variable-Length Quizzes: If you want the loop to adapt to the selected quiz size, then in Turn 4 replace @TOTAL_QUESTIONS@ with @CURRENT_QUIZ[N]@ (so REPEAT iterates based on the array length).
    
- To Add a GAMSA Tutor Summary: If you want narrative feedback, then append a new LLM turn after Turn 7 that takes the Turn 7 summary content as input and returns an “AI Tutor” explanation.
    
- To Switch from Static Bank to OMEGA: If you want on-the-fly quiz generation, then replace the static QUIZ_BANK filing step with an initial LLM turn that generates the CURRENT_QUIZ JSON array, and then start execution at the loop setup (current Turn 4).
    
- To Capture Rationale per Question: If you want SCREAM-style diagnostics, then extend the JP schema to include rationale_prompt per question and modify Turn 5 to use the 4-argument RADIO form to collect the user’s reasoning.

# Intake Router with Dynamic Personas: Constrained Intent Classifier + Symbolic Persona Hot-Swap

## Metadata

- Framework: IMPACT
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Intake Routing (Safety-Critical Triage + Administrative Handling)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: TEXTAREA, SET, MAP, TR, TN
    
- Key Concepts: Persona Ontology (pre-built system prompts), LLM constrained classification (output-values), Deterministic persona routing (MAP with default N+1 case), System-prompt indirection (@@SelectedPersona@@)
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: A single static persona is unsafe and inefficient in healthcare intake; urgent symptoms, administrative requests, and non-urgent symptoms require different guardrails and actions.
    
- Core Mechanism: Collects user complaint, uses an LLM to classify intent into one of three allowed keys, symbolically maps that key to a pre-audited persona parameter name, then dynamically loads that persona as the system prompt to generate the final response.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{  

    "options": {  

        "title": "Medical Intake Router (Refined 3-Case Model)",  

        "name": "Medical Triage Router - Refined 3-Case",  

        "brief": "Classifies user symptoms as Urgent, New Symptom, or Administrative to load a dynamic medical persona.",  

        "description": "This agent classifies a user's medical complaint. It uses the MAP command to map this classification to a 'Triage Nurse', 'Receptionist', or 'Nurse Practitioner' persona. The final LLM turn uses this dynamic persona (@@SelectedPersona@@) to reply.",  

        "greeting": "Welcome to the virtual clinic. Please describe your symptoms or your question in detail.",  

        "params": {  

            "CLASSIFIER_PERSONA": {  

                "org": "You are an expert medical triage classifier. Read the user's request. Your goal is to determine the intent. Your response MUST be ONLY one word: 'Urgent', 'New Symptom', or 'Administrative'.\n- 'Urgent': User mentions severe pain, difficulty breathing, chest pain, uncontrolled bleeding, or sounds highly distressed.\n- 'Administrative': User is asking about appointments, billing, prescription refills, test results, or insurance.\n- 'New Symptom': User is describing any other non-emergency medical symptom (e.g., cough, rash, mild pain, check-up request).",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "The system prompt for the LLM classifier."  

            },  

            "INTENT_KEYS": {  

                "org": "Urgent|Administrative|New Symptom",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "The allowed outputs for the LLM classifier, used in output-values."  

            },  

            "TRIAGE_NURSE_PERSONA": {  

                "org": "You are a Triage Nurse. The user's symptoms sound 'Urgent'. **Your response MUST NOT provide medical advice.** Your ONLY task is to instruct the user to seek immediate, real-world medical help. State clearly: 'Based on your description, this sounds like an emergency. Please call 911 or go to your nearest emergency room immediately.'",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "Persona for handling urgent issues. Includes a safety rail."  

            },  

            "RECEPTIONIST_PERSONA": {  

                "org": "You are a Medical Receptionist. The user has an 'Administrative' question (e.g., billing, scheduling, refills). Do not discuss symptoms. Respond politely and route them to the correct department. Example: 'I can help with that. For appointments or refills, please call our main office at 555-1234. For billing questions, please call 555-5678.'",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "Persona for handling billing/appointment/refill questions."  

            },  

            "NURSE_PRACTITIONER_PERSONA": {  

                "org": "You are a Nurse Practitioner. The user has a 'New Symptom'. Respond with empathy. **Do not diagnose.** Your goal is to gather more information for their file and book an appointment. Thank them for the details. State that a follow-up is needed. Example: 'Thank you for describing your symptoms. I've noted them down. This sounds like something we should discuss further. I can help you book the next available appointment.'",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "Persona for handling non-urgent new symptoms."  

            }  

        }  

    },  

    "prompts": [  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T1: Get the user's medical complaint.\n@TEXTAREA(\"user_complaint\", \"Please describe your symptoms or question:\")@",  

            "show": true,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "@CLASSIFIER_PERSONA@",  

            "user": "@TEXTAREA(user_complaint)@",  

            "temperature": "0.1",  

            "max-tokens": "50",  

            "show": true,  

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano",  

            "output-values": "@INTENT_KEYS@"  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T3: (Router) Map classification from T2 to a Persona Parameter name using MAP.\n@SET(SelectedPersona, \"@MAP(\"@TR@TN(-1)@@\", \"Urgent|Administrative\", \"TRIAGE_NURSE_PERSONA|RECEPTIONIST_PERSONA|NURSE_PRACTITIONER_PERSONA\")@\")@",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "@@SelectedPersona@@",  

            "user": "Original Complaint:\n@TEXTAREA(user_complaint)@",  

            "temperature": "0.1",  

            "max-tokens": "2000",  

            "show": true,  

            "markdown": true,  

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano"  

        }  

    ]  

}

  

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- CLASSIFIER_PERSONA: Classifier system prompt defining the 3 mutually exclusive intent classes and enforcing single-token output.
    
- INTENT_KEYS: Pipe list used as output-values guardrail for Turn 2.
    
- TRIAGE_NURSE_PERSONA: Urgent-case persona with strict “no medical advice” constraint and emergency escalation instruction.
    
- RECEPTIONIST_PERSONA: Administrative-case persona for scheduling/billing/refills routing; excludes symptom discussion.
    
- NURSE_PRACTITIONER_PERSONA: Default persona for non-urgent symptoms; gathers info and suggests appointment; prohibits diagnosis.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic, UI): Captures user free-text complaint via TEXTAREA(user_complaint).
    
- Turn 2 (LLM, UI): Classifies complaint into exactly one of Urgent|Administrative|New Symptom using output-values guardrail.
    
- Turn 3 (Symbolic): Routes intent → persona parameter name using MAP with default case:
    

- If Urgent → TRIAGE_NURSE_PERSONA
    
- If Administrative → RECEPTIONIST_PERSONA
    
- Else (i.e., New Symptom) → NURSE_PRACTITIONER_PERSONA (N+1 default)
    

- Turn 4 (LLM, UI): “Hot-swaps” system prompt using indirection @@SelectedPersona@@ and responds using the original complaint as input.

  C --> D[Turn 3: SET SelectedPersona = MAP(intent -> persona param)]

  D --> E[Turn 4: LLM Response<br/>system = @@SelectedPersona@@]

  E --> F[End]

- Structure Related:  
    “Create an intake workflow: TEXTAREA → constrained classifier → symbolic router → dynamic persona execution.”
    
- Complexity Related:  
    “Generate an advanced safety-critical router with a default persona case.”
    

### Usage & Modification Requests

- Task Related:  
    “Add a fourth intent (Follow-up) with a new persona, keeping the 4-turn structure.”
    
- Reuse:  
    “Reuse this dynamic persona router for IT helpdesk (Urgent outage vs. ticketing vs. how-to).”
    
- Bounded Changes:  
    “Change only the classifier wording without adding turns.”
    

Modification Recipes (If/Then):

- To Add a 4th Intent: If you add Follow-up to INTENT_KEYS, then update CLASSIFIER_PERSONA to define it and update Turn 3’s MAP value_list/return_list to include the new routing target persona.
    
- To Log Complaints + Routing: If you need auditability, then insert a hidden symbolic turn after Turn 4 that calls @SAVE(...)@ with the complaint and the classification key.
    
- To Route to Other Agents: If you want full handoff instead of persona swapping, then change Turn 3 to map to agent IDs/URLs (not persona param names) and make Turn 4 a symbolic handoff/redirect constructor.

# JSON Loop Quiz Generator: Generate–Fix–Store–Administer via Aggregated JSON Objects

## Metadata

- Framework: IOTA
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Assessment (Dynamic Quiz Generation + Deterministic Administration)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: TEXT, REPEAT, SETJ, RADIO, MAP, TR, TN
    
- Key Concepts: Hybrid generation loop, output-values JSON schema contract, Platform JSON-object aggregation into array, LLM “fixer” utility pass, JP array indexing aligned with @R_i@
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: LLMs can generate rich quiz content but cannot be trusted to consistently emit perfectly parsable structures for downstream symbolic commands.
    
- Core Mechanism: Repeats an LLM turn to generate multiple single-item JSON objects under a strict schema, relies on automatic aggregation into a JSON array, runs a second LLM “fixer” to guarantee valid array structure, stores the validated array into a JP via SETJ, then administers and grades each item deterministically via RADIO + MAP inside a second REPEAT loop.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{  

    "options": {  

        "title": "Dynamic Topic Quiz Generator (JSON Loop)",  

        "brief": "Generates quiz items for any user-provided topic using a JSON loop and aggregates them.",  

        "name": "Generic JSON Loop Generator",  

        "description": "This agent asks for a topic. It uses a REPEAT loop to generate 3 quiz items as JSON objects, runs them through an LLM fixer, and then administers the quiz.",  

        "greeting": "Welcome! I can generate a quiz on any subject you choose. What topic would you like to test?",  

        "params": {  

            "NUM_STEPS": {  

                "org": "3",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "Number of quiz items to generate."  

            },  

            "GENERATOR_PERSONA": {  

                "org": "You are an expert educator and quiz master. Based on the topic provided, generate a unique and challenging quiz item. Your output MUST be a valid JSON object with three keys: 'question' (string), 'options' (a pipe-separated string of 4 choices), and 'answer' (the correct choice string). Do not output a list, just a single object.",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "Persona for generating single JSON objects for any domain."  

            },  

            "JSON_SCHEMA": {  

                "org": "{\"question\":\"<string>\",\"options\":\"<string|string|string|string>\",\"answer\":\"<string>\"}",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "Schema constraint for the LLM output."  

            },  

            "FIXER_PERSONA": {  

                "org": "You are a data formatting utility. You will receive a string of concatenated JSON objects (e.g., {obj}{obj}{obj}) or a potentially malformed array. Your ONLY task is to parse this input and return a single, valid JSON array (e.g., [{obj},{obj},{obj}]). Do not add or change any content, just fix the structure.",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "Persona for the LLM-based JSON fixer."  

            }  

        }  

    },  

    "prompts": [  

        {  

            "user": "/ T1: Ask the user for the topic.\n@TEXT(\"user_topic\", \"Enter the topic (e.g., Quantum Physics, 90s Music):\")@",  

            "show": true  

        },  

        {  

            "user": "/ T2: Setup the generation loop to run T3 exactly 3 times.\n@REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(1)@, \"@NUM_STEPS@\")@",  

            "show": false  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "@GENERATOR_PERSONA@",  

            "user": "Topic: @TEXT(user_topic)@\nGenerate quiz item number @R_i@.",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano",  

            "temperature": "0.7",  

            "output-values": "@JSON_SCHEMA@"  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "@FIXER_PERSONA@",  

            "user": "@TR@TN(-1)@@",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano",  

            "temperature": "0.1"  

        },  

        {  

            "user": "/ T5: Store the clean, fixed JSON array (from T4) into a JSON Parameter (SETJ).\n@SETJ(QUIZ_DATA, @TR@TN(-1)@@)@",  

            "show": false  

        },  

        {  

            "user": "/ T6: Setup the administration loop to run T7 and T8 for each item in the array.\n@REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(2)@, \"@NUM_STEPS@\")@",  

            "show": false  

        },  

        {  

            "user": "/ T7 (LOOP 1/2): Display the question using data from the JSON Parameter.\n@RADIO(\"ans_@R_i@\", \"Question @R_i@: @QUIZ_DATA[@R_i@].question@\", \"@QUIZ_DATA[@R_i@].options@\")@",  

            "show": true  

        },  

        {  

            "user": "/ T8 (LOOP 2/2): Grade the answer using MAP and the stored correct answer.\n@MAP(\"@RADIO(ans_@R_i@)@\", \"@QUIZ_DATA[@R_i@].answer@\", \"Correct!|Incorrect. The answer was @QUIZ_DATA[@R_i@].answer@.\")@",  

            "show": true  

        },  

        {  

            "user": "/ T9: Final message.\nQuiz complete! Feel free to restart and choose a new topic.",  

            "markdown": true,  

            "show": true  

        }  

    ]  

}

  

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- NUM_STEPS: Controls both generation loop length (Turn 2) and administration loop length (Turn 6).
    
- GENERATOR_PERSONA: Forces “single JSON object per iteration” content generation role.
    
- JSON_SCHEMA: Output contract used in output-values to constrain Turn 3 to a strict object shape, including RADIO-compatible pipe options.
    
- FIXER_PERSONA: Utility persona to normalize/repair aggregated outputs into a single valid JSON array without content changes.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic, UI): Gets user topic via TEXT(user_topic).
    
- Turn 2 (Symbolic): REPEAT runs Turn 3 exactly NUM_STEPS times.
    
- Turn 3 (LLM, Hidden, Loop): Generates one quiz-item JSON object per iteration under output-values: JSON_SCHEMA.
    
- Turn 4 (LLM, Hidden): Fixes/validates the loop output into a single valid JSON array.
    
- Turn 5 (Symbolic): Stores validated array into JP QUIZ_DATA via SETJ (unquoted args).
    
- Turn 6 (Symbolic): REPEAT runs Turns 7–8 for each quiz item.
    
- Turn 7 (Symbolic, UI, Loop): Asks the question using JP access QUIZ_DATA[@R_i@].question and options.
    
- Turn 8 (Symbolic, UI, Loop): Grades with MAP(user_choice, correct_answer, feedback_pair).
    
- Turn 9 (Symbolic, UI): Completion message.
    

## Visualization Mermaid Code

graph TD

  A[Start] --> B[Turn 1: TEXT user_topic]

  B --> C{Turn 2: REPEAT (Generate) x NUM_STEPS}

  C --> D[Turn 3: LLM Generate 1 JSON object<br/>output-values = JSON_SCHEMA]

  D --> C

  C --> E[Turn 4: LLM Fixer -> Valid JSON Array]

  E --> F[Turn 5: SETJ QUIZ_DATA = fixed array]

  F --> G{Turn 6: REPEAT (Administer) x NUM_STEPS}

  G --> H[Turn 7: RADIO from QUIZ_DATA[Ri]]

  H --> I[Turn 8: MAP grade vs QUIZ_DATA[Ri].answer]

  I --> G

  G --> J[Turn 9: Final message]

  J --> K[End]

  

## Related Questions and Instructions

### Design & Architecture Requests

- Framework Related:  
    “Generate a MACRO agent that uses a JSON contract (output-values) to safely bridge LLM generation into symbolic quiz delivery.”
    
- Structure Related:  
    “Create a REPEAT-based generator loop that aggregates JSON objects into an array and then stores it with SETJ.”
    
- Complexity Related:  
    “Generate an advanced hybrid agent using an LLM ‘fixer’ utility pass before symbolic execution.”
    

### Usage & Modification Requests

- Task Related:  
    “Increase NUM_STEPS to 10 and keep the same Generate→Fix→Store→Administer flow.”
    
- Reuse:  
    “Reuse this JSON loop generator to create flashcards (front/back) instead of multiple choice.”
    
- Bounded Changes:  
    “Change only the generator persona and JSON schema fields without adding turns.”
    

Modification Recipes (If/Then):

- To Add Scoring: If you need a numeric score, then add USER_SCORE as an AP initialized before Turn 6, and insert a hidden scoring turn after Turn 8 that maps Correct/Incorrect to 1|0 and increments via EVAL.
    
- To Make Item Count User-Controlled: If you want the user to choose the number of questions, then add a new input control for item count and use that value in place of NUM_STEPS in Turns 2 and 6.
    
- To Export as an IOTA Module: If you want this to be an item factory only, then remove Turns 6–9 and end after storing QUIZ_DATA (optionally saving it as a DID via SAVE) for downstream agents.
    

## References

- Choi, J. (2025). JSON Loop Quiz Generator: Generate–Fix–Store–Administer via Aggregated JSON Objects. In Collective AI on the Foundation AI (CAFA): The pathway of digital transformation of intelligence. CAFA Lab, Inc.

# 2-Param Stem with Parallel Enumeration List using IOTA Framework: Linked P1/P2 Stem Assembly + P3 Answer Bank

## Metadata

- Framework: IOTA
    
- Complexity: Intermediate
    
- Primary Function: Assessment Item Generation (Item Factory)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: REPEAT, D, SETJ, RADIO, TR, TN
    
- Key Concepts: Parallel enumeration lists, SHUFFLE + LINK alignment, 2-parameter stem template, Distractor generation from answer pool, JSON item bank compilation, Optional human validation loop
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Many assessment items require a stem composed from two linked attributes (e.g., Subject + Attribute) while mapping to a single correct answer; maintaining pairing integrity during randomization is error-prone.
    
- Core Mechanism: Uses a 10-item ontology of linked parallel lists where P1 is shuffled and P2/P3 are LINKed to P1. A REPEAT loop enumerates instances, builds each item’s JSON (prompt from P1+P2; correctAnswer from P3), generates choices using @D() from the pooled answers, compiles all items into one JSON array, then stores it as a JP artifact (assessmentTest) with an optional validation loop.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{  

    "options": {  

        "title": "IOTA Example: General Knowledge Item",  

        "brief": "A dynamic item generator that uses a 10-item parallel ontology (2 for stem, 1 for answer).",  

        "name": "IOTA - AIG Item Template - 2-Param Stem (10-Item)",  

        "description": "This IOTA agent uses parallel lists (P1, P2, P3). The stem is generated from P1 and P2, and the answer is from P3. It compiles the generated items into a JSON array and provides an optional validation loop.",  

        "greeting": "Welcome to the IOTA Item Generator. This agent will create a set of general knowledge problems.",  

        "params": {  

            "P1": {  

                "org": "William Shakespeare|J.R.R. Tolkien|Isaac Newton|Leonardo da Vinci|Albert Einstein|Marie Curie|Vincent van Gogh|Ludwig van Beethoven|Galileo Galilei|Charles Darwin",  

                "cond": "SHUFFLE",  

                "desc": "Parameter 1: The 'Subject' (e.g., Author/Scientist). This list is shuffled."  

            },  

            "P2": {  

                "org": "most famous play|most famous novel|most famous law|most famous painting|most famous equation|pioneering research field|most famous painting|most famous symphony|most famous astronomical observation|most famous theory",  

                "cond": "LINK(P1)",  

                "desc": "Parameter 2: The 'Attribute' (e.g., Work Type). Linked to P1."  

            },  

            "P3": {  

                "org": "Hamlet|The Lord of the Rings|The law of universal gravitation|Mona Lisa|E=mc²|Radioactivity|The Starry Night|Symphony No. 5|Moons of Jupiter|Theory of Evolution",  

                "cond": "LINK(P1)",  

                "desc": "Parameter 3: The 'Answer'. Linked to P1 to maintain the correct relationship."  

            },  

            "prompt": {  

                "org": "What is @P1[@R_i@]@'s @P2[@R_i@]@?",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "The template for the question stem, using P1 and P2."  

            },  

            "correctAnswer": {  

                "org": "@P3[@R_i@]@",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "The template for the correct answer, pulled from the linked P3 list."  

            },  

            "choices": {  

                "org": "@P3@",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "The pool of potential distractors (all answers). The @D() command will pull from this."  

            },  

            "numberOfChoices": {  

                "org": "4",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "The total number of choices (1 correct + 3 distractors) for each item."  

            },  

            "numberOfInstances": {  

                "org": "10",  

                "cond": "SELF",  

                "desc": "The total number of unique item instances to generate."  

            }  

        }  

    },  

    "prompts": [  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T1: This hidden control turn sets up the REPEAT loop to generate all item instances (T2 and T3).\n@REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(2)@, \"@numberOfInstances@\")@",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T2 (LOOP 1/2): Generate the JSON string for a single item instance. This runs N times.\n{\"identifier\":\"Insatance_@R_i@\",\"prompt\":\"@prompt@\",\"choices\":\"@D(\"@correctAnswer@\", \"\", \"@choices@\", \"@numberOfChoices@\", \"ASCE\")@\",\"correctAnswer\":\"@correctAnswer@\"}",  

            "show": true,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T3 (LOOP 2/2): Store the JSON string from T2 into a unique JSON Parameter (e.g., Insatance_1).\n@SETJ(Insatance_@R_i@, @TR@TN(-1)[@R_i@]@)@",  

            "show": true,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "You are provided with @numberOfInstances@ JSON objects, concatenated as a raw string. Your task is to compile them into a valid JSON array, starting with [ and ending with ]. Provide ONLY the raw JSON array, without any other text or markdown wrappers.",  

            "user": "@TR@TN(-2)@@",  

            "show": true,  

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano"  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T5: Store the final, complete JSON array from the LLM into the 'assessmentTest' parameter.\n@SETJ(assessmentTest, @TR@TN(-1)@@)@",  

            "show": true,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T6: This hidden turn sets up an optional REPEAT loop to validate the generated items.\n@REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(1)@, \"@numberOfInstances@\")@",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T7 (VALIDATION LOOP): Display each item from the 'assessmentTest' JSON array using a RADIO control for human validation.\n@RADIO(R_@R_i@, \"@assessmentTest[@R_i@].prompt@\", \"@assessmentTest[@R_i@].choices@\")@",  

            "show": true,  

            "model": null  

        }  

    ]  

}

  

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- P1: Primary subject list; cond: SHUFFLE randomizes item order per session.
    
- P2: Attribute list; cond: LINK(P1) keeps attribute aligned to shuffled subjects.
    
- P3: Answer list; cond: LINK(P1) ensures correctAnswer remains aligned to the subject–attribute pair.
    
- prompt: Stem template combining two parameters (P1 + P2) at loop index @R_i@.
    
- correctAnswer: Answer template pulling from P3 at @R_i@.
    
- choices: Distractor pool defined as the full P3 list.
    
- numberOfChoices: Choice count for @D() (1 correct + distractors).
    
- numberOfInstances: Loop length; generates one item per ontology row.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic, Hidden): Starts generation loop across instances with REPEAT (runs Turns 2–3).
    
- Turn 2 (Symbolic, Visible, Loop): Constructs one JSON object string for the current instance, including:
    

- prompt assembled from @prompt@ (P1+P2)
    
- choices generated by @D(correctAnswer, "", choices, numberOfChoices, "ASCE")@
    
- correctAnswer from P3
    

- Turn 3 (Symbolic, Visible, Loop): Stores each per-instance JSON string into a distinct JP (Insatance_@R_i@) using SETJ.
    
- Turn 4 (LLM, Visible): Compiles concatenated JSON objects into a single valid JSON array (formatting utility role).
    
- Turn 5 (Symbolic, Visible): Stores the final JSON array into assessmentTest via SETJ.
    
- Turn 6 (Symbolic, Hidden): Optional validation loop setup across numberOfInstances.
    
- Turn 7 (Symbolic, Visible, Loop): Human validation UI: displays each assessmentTest[@R_i@] as a RADIO.
    

## Visualization Mermaid Code

graph TD

  A[Start] --> B[Turn 1: REPEAT x numberOfInstances<br/>(runs Turns 2-3)]

  B --> C[Turn 2 (Loop): Build item JSON string<br/>prompt=P1+P2, answer=P3, choices=@D()]

  C --> D[Turn 3 (Loop): SETJ Insatance_Ri = item JSON]

  D --> B

  B --> E[Turn 4: LLM compile raw objects -> JSON array]

  E --> F[Turn 5: SETJ assessmentTest = final array]

  F --> G[Turn 6: Optional REPEAT validation loop]

  G --> H[Turn 7 (Loop): RADIO display assessmentTest[Ri]]

  H --> G

  G --> I[End]

  

## Related Questions and Instructions

### Design & Architecture Requests

- Framework Related:  
    “Generate an IOTA agent that produces a JSON item bank using linked parallel lists and a two-field stem template.”
    
- Structure Related:  
    “Create an item factory where P2 and P3 are LINKed to a SHUFFLEd P1.”
    
- Complexity Related:  
    “Generate an intermediate IOTA that uses @D() for distractors and outputs a compiled JSON array.”
    

### Usage & Modification Requests

- Task Related:  
    “Replace the subject/attribute/answer ontology with a different domain (e.g., diseases + test type → recommended test).”
    
- Reuse:  
    “Reuse this structure to generate vocabulary items: word + part-of-speech → definition.”
    
- Bounded Changes:  
    “Change numberOfChoices from 4 to 5 without adding turns.”
    

Modification Recipes (If/Then):

- To Add Rationales: If you want explanations, then add a new linked parameter P4 with cond: LINK(P1) and include "rationale":"@P4[@R_i@]@" inside Turn 2’s JSON.
    
- To Remove Validation UI: If you want a pure factory-only IOTA, then remove Turns 6–7 (optional loop) and end after Turn 5 storing assessmentTest.
    
- To Change Distractor Strategy: If you want different ordering, then adjust the final argument of @D(..., "ASCE")@ (keeping the command structure unchanged).
    

## References

# Integer Division Quiz with Parallel Lists using IOTA Framework: Pre-Validated Dividend/Divisor Pairs + Linked Integer Answers

## Metadata

- Framework: IOTA
    
- Complexity: Intermediate
    
- Primary Function: Assessment Item Generation (Item Factory for Integer-Division MCQs)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: REPEAT, D, SETJ, RADIO, TR, TN
    
- Key Concepts: Full enumeration via parallel lists, SHUFFLE + LINK integrity, Avoiding non-integer division outputs, JSON item bank compilation, Optional validation loop
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Division item generation via on-the-fly calculation risks non-integer quotients (e.g., 10/3), which breaks simple multiple-choice integer-division quizzes.
    
- Core Mechanism: Pre-defines only valid integer-division triples (P1 dividend, P2 divisor, P3 quotient) and uses LINK(P1) to keep each divisor and answer aligned to its shuffled dividend; then iterates through this validated ontology to assemble MCQ items and compile them into a reusable JSON array artifact.

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "You are provided with @numberOfInstances@ JSON objects, concatenated as a raw string. Your task is to compile them into a valid JSON array, starting with [ and ending with ]. Provide ONLY the raw JSON array, without any other text or markdown wrappers.",  

            "user": "@TR@TN(-2)@@",  

            "show": true,  

            "model": "gpt-4.1-nano"  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T5: Store the final, complete JSON array from the LLM into the 'assessmentTest' parameter.\n@SETJ(assessmentTest, @TR@TN(-1)@@)@",  

            "show": true,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T6: This hidden turn sets up an optional REPEAT loop to validate the generated items.\n@REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(1)@, \"@numberOfInstances@\")@",  

            "show": false,  

            "model": null  

        },  

        {  

            "system": "",  

            "user": "/ T7 (VALIDATION LOOP): Display each item from the 'assessmentTest' JSON array using a RADIO control for human validation.\n@RADIO(R_@R_i@, \"@assessmentTest[@R_i@].prompt@\", \"@assessmentTest[@R_i@].choices@\")@",  

            "show": true,  

            "model": null  

        }  

    ]  

}

  

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- P1 (Dividend): Shuffled master list that drives instance order.
    
- P2 (Divisor): LINK(P1) ensures the divisor stays paired to the shuffled dividend.
    
- P3 (Quotient): LINK(P1) ensures the integer answer stays paired to the shuffled dividend.
    
- prompt: Stem template combining P1 and P2 at index @R_i@.
    
- correctAnswer: Answer template from P3 at @R_i@.
    
- choices: Distractor pool set to the full set of quotients (@P3@).
    
- numberOfChoices / numberOfInstances: Control choice count and number of generated items.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic, Hidden): REPEAT runs Turns 2–3 for numberOfInstances.
    
- Turn 2 (Symbolic, Loop): Assembles one item JSON string, using @D() to produce a 4-option choice set containing the correct quotient plus distractors from choices.
    
- Turn 3 (Symbolic, Loop): Stores each per-instance item as its own JP (Insatance_@R_i@) using SETJ for debugging/inspection.
    
- Turn 4 (LLM): Compiles concatenated JSON objects into a valid JSON array.
    
- Turn 5 (Symbolic): Stores compiled array into JP assessmentTest.
    
- Turn 6–7 (Symbolic, Optional): Validation REPEAT displays each generated item from assessmentTest in a RADIO control.

  C --> D[Turn 3 (Loop): SETJ Insatance_Ri]

  F --> G[Turn 6: Optional validation REPEAT]

## Related Questions and Instructions

### Design & Architecture Requests

- Framework Related:  
    “Generate an IOTA agent that guarantees integer arithmetic by using linked parallel lists instead of EVAL.”
    
- Structure Related:  
    “Create a 3-list ontology (dividend/divisor/quotient) with SHUFFLE + LINK integrity and output a JSON item bank.”
    
- Complexity Related:  
    “Generate an intermediate IOTA with an optional RADIO validation loop.”
    

### Usage & Modification Requests

- Task Related:  
    “Swap the ontology to fraction-reduction items while preserving the same linked-list template.”
    
- Reuse:  
    “Reuse this parallel-list structure for unit conversions (value/unit → converted value).”
    
- Bounded Changes:  
    “Change numberOfChoices to 5 without adding turns.”
    

Modification Recipes (If/Then):

- To Expand the Ontology Safely: If you add more division problems, then append new aligned entries to P1/P2/P3 and keep LINK(P1) on P2 and P3 so shuffling preserves correctness.
    
- To Add Explanations: If you want rationales, then add P4 with cond: LINK(P1) and include "rationale":"@P4[@R_i@]@" in Turn 2’s JSON.
    
- To Remove LLM Compilation: If you want fully symbolic output only, then remove Turn 4 and instead rely on per-instance JPs (Insatance_@R_i@) as the generated artifact (keeping the rest unchanged).

# Generative Stem - Division using IOTA Framework: LLM-in-Loop Word Problems + Linked Integer Division Ontology

## Metadata

- Framework: IOTA
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Assessment Item Generation (Hybrid AIG: Symbolic Answers + Generative Stems)
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: REPEAT, SETJ, D, RADIO, TR, TN, LINK, SHUFFLE
    
- Key Concepts: Parallel lists for integer-division integrity, SHUFFLE+LINK alignment, LLM-in-the-loop stem generation, Random template selection via Stem_Template[.], JSON item compilation + storage as JP, Optional validation loop
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved: Division items must keep integer answers (symbolic reliability), but static stems become repetitive and less engaging at scale.
    
- Core Mechanism: Uses a validated parallel-list ontology (P1/P2/P3) for deterministic math correctness, while an LLM inside the generation loop creates varied word-problem stems guided by a randomly selected, shuffled style template; then assembles each item into JSON and compiles the full bank into assessmentTest.

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params):

- P1: Dividend list (SHUFFLE) defines randomized instance order.
    
- P2: Divisor list (LINK(P1)) preserves correct dividend–divisor pairing after shuffle.
    
- P3: Quotient list (LINK(P1)) preserves integer answer alignment after shuffle.
    
- Stem_Template: Five style guides (SHUFFLE) for randomized stem variety; accessed per iteration via @Stem_Template[.]@.
    
- STEM_GENERATOR_PERSONA: LLM system prompt enforcing “output only stem text” and integer-answer requirement.
    
- choices / numberOfChoices / numberOfInstances: Distractor pool, option count, and instance count controls.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array):

- Turn 1 (Symbolic, Hidden): REPEAT runs Turns 2–4 for each instance (10 iterations).
    
- Turn 2 (LLM, Hidden, In-Loop): Generates one word-problem stem using current P1/P2 values plus a randomly selected style guide from Stem_Template[.].
    
- Turn 3 (Symbolic, Visible, In-Loop): Assembles item JSON using:
    

- prompt from prior LLM output (@TR@TN(-1)[@R_i@]@)
    
- correctAnswer from P3 (@P3[@R_i@]@)
    
- choices via @D(correct, "", pool, numberOfChoices, "ASCE")@
    

- Turn 4 (Symbolic, Hidden, In-Loop): Stores each item JSON into a per-instance JP (Instance_@R_i@) using SETJ.
    
- Turn 5 (LLM, Visible): Compiles concatenated objects into a single valid JSON array.
    
- Turn 6 (Symbolic, Hidden): Stores the compiled array into JP assessmentTest using SETJ.
    
- Turn 7–8 (Symbolic, Optional): Validation loop displays each generated item from assessmentTest using RADIO.

### Design & Architecture Requests

- Framework Related:

- Structure Related:

Modification Recipes (If/Then):

- To Add More Stem Styles: If you need more variation, then append new style strings to Stem_Template.org and keep cond: SHUFFLE so per-iteration selection remains randomized.
    
- To Make Stems Deterministic: If you want fixed stems (no LLM), then replace Turn 2 with a symbolic stem template parameter (e.g., prompt) and have Turn 3 reference that parameter instead of @TR...@.
    
- To Store the Generated Stem Separately: If you want explicit stem logging, then insert a hidden symbolic @SET(STEM_@R_i@, "@TR@TN(-1)[@R_i@]@")@ immediately after Turn 2 (inside the loop), before Turn 3.

# Division Quiz with a Symbolic Cognitive Distractor Generation Model using IOTA Framework

## Metadata

- Framework: IOTA (Item Ontology Model-based Template Agent)
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Assessment Item Generation & Diagnostic Feedback
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: REPEAT, SET, SETJ, EVAL, D, MAP, RADIO
    
- Key Concepts: Parallel Lists (Full Enumeration), Cognitive Distractor Modeling, Rich JSON Artifacts, Dual REPEAT Loops, Symbolic–LLM Hybrid
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved:  
    Randomized division item generation using direct evaluation often produces non-integer answers and pedagogically weak distractors, undermining assessment validity and feedback quality.
    
- Core Mechanism:  
    This agent uses parallel lists (P1/P2/P3) to guarantee valid integer division items, dynamically generates cognitively meaningful distractors via symbolic EVAL operations, and combines them with static rationales to deliver diagnostic feedback through a structured JSON assessment artifact.

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params)

- P1 / P2 / P3: Parallel lists implementing full enumeration to preserve valid integer division and correct answers under shuffling.
    
- Distractor_Rationales: Static explanatory ontology aligned positionally with dynamically generated distractors.
    
- prompt / correctAnswer: IOTA templates resolved per loop index.
    
- numberOfInstances: Controls both generation and validation loops.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array)

- Turn 1 (Symbolic): Initializes REPEAT loop for item generation.
    
- Turn 2 (Symbolic): Generates cognitively motivated distractors via EVAL.
    
- Turn 3 (Symbolic): Assembles per-item “rich JSON” string.
    
- Turn 4 (Symbolic): Stores each instance JSON via SETJ.
    
- Turn 5 (LLM): Compiles concatenated JSON strings into a valid array.
    
- Turn 6 (Symbolic): Stores final assessmentTest artifact.
    
- Turn 7 (Symbolic): Initializes validation REPEAT loop.
    
- Turn 8 (Symbolic): Presents item using RADIO control.
    
- Turn 9 (Symbolic): Grades response with MAP.
    
- Turn 10 (Symbolic): Extracts distractors into indexable AP.
    
- Turn 11 (Symbolic): Displays correctness and diagnostic distractor feedback.

- Reuse:  
    “Reuse this IOTA structure with different numeric ontologies.”
    
- Bounded Changes:  
    “Replace cognitive distractors with random numeric distractors only.”

# Generative Cognitive Distractor Model using LLM-in-the-Loop Parsing using IOTA Framework

## Metadata

- Framework: IOTA (with OMEGA-style LLM emulation inside loop)
    
- Complexity: Advanced
    
- Primary Function: Assessment Item Generation + Cognitive Distractors + Diagnostic Feedback
    
- Key Symbolic Commands: REPEAT, SET, SETJ, JSONVALS, D, RADIO, MAP, TN, TR
    
- Key Concepts: LLM-in-the-loop generation, Markdown→JSON parsing chain, Per-item JSON Parameters, Rich JSON artifacts, Dual-loop architecture
    

## Background & Objective

- Problem Solved:  
    Static distractor pools often fail to produce high-quality cognitive distractors (common-error answers) and cannot adapt distractors/rationales to each specific item instance.
    
- Core Mechanism:  
    Uses a “Generate → Parse → Store → Assemble” pipeline inside the IOTA generation loop: an LLM generates a 5-row Markdown distractor table, a second LLM converts it into a strict JSON array, symbolic turns store and extract distractor values, and the final item JSON embeds the full distractor rationale data for downstream validation feedback.
    

## Full CAFA Agent Code

{

  "options": {

    "title": "IOTA: Generative Cognitive Distractor Model (5 Distractors)",

    "brief": "An IOTA agent that uses an LLM-in-the-loop to generate, parse, and use 5 cognitive distractors.",

    "name": "IOTA - Generative Distractor (Markdown-to-JSON) v3",

    "description": "This agent generates quiz items from an ontology (Stem, Answer). Inside the loop, it uses one LLM to generate 5 distractors as Markdown, a second LLM to parse the Markdown into JSON, and then stores and uses that JSON to build the final item. The validation loop now grades the user and shows the 5 distractor rationales.",

    "greeting": "Welcome! This agent will generate a 3-item quiz, creating 5 cognitive distractors for each item.",

    "params": {

      "Stem_Feature": {

        "org": "What is 12 / 3?|What is 20 / 4?|What is 50 / 10?|What is 18 / 9?|What is 40 / 8?",

        "cond": "SHUFFLE",

        "desc": "Parameter 1: The 'Stem' (Question). This list is shuffled."

      },

      "Answer_Feature": {

        "org": "4|5|5|2|5",

        "cond": "LINK(Stem_Feature)",

        "desc": "Parameter 2: The 'Answer'. Linked to Stem_Feature."

      },

      "P1_Values": {

        "org": "12|20|50|18|40",

        "cond": "LINK(Stem_Feature)",

        "desc": "Parallel data for P1 (Dividend), linked for generation."

      },

      "P2_Values": {

        "org": "3|4|10|9|8",

        "cond": "LINK(Stem_Feature)",

        "desc": "Parallel data for P2 (Divisor), linked for generation."

      },

      "DISTRACTOR_GENERATOR_PERSONA": {

        "org": "You are an expert math teacher. For the given division problem, generate *exactly 5* plausible cognitive distractors based on common student errors (e.g., adding, subtracting, multiplying, off-by-one). Your response MUST be ONLY a Markdown table with *exactly 5 data rows* (plus a header row), and two columns: 'Distractor' and 'Rationale'. Do not generate 3 or 4. You must generate 5. Do not include any other text.",

        "cond": "SELF"

      },

      "JSON_PARSER_PERSONA": {

        "org": "You are a data formatting utility. Convert the provided Markdown table (which should have 5 data rows) into a valid JSON array of objects. Your response MUST be ONLY the raw JSON array, with no other text, comments, or markdown wrappers. Ensure all 5 objects are in the array.",

        "cond": "SELF"

      },

      "numberOfInstances": {

        "org": "3",

        "cond": "SELF",

        "desc": "The total number of unique item instances to generate."

      }

    }

  },

  "prompts": [

    {

      "system": "",

      "user": "/ T1: Setup REPEAT loop to generate N items (T2-T6).\\n@REPEAT(@TN(1)@, @TN(5)@, @numberOfInstances@)@",

      "show": false,

      "model": null

    },

    {

      "system": "@DISTRACTOR_GENERATOR_PERSONA@",

      "user": "Problem: @Stem_Feature[@R_i@]@\\nCorrect Answer: @Answer_Feature[@R_i@]@\\n(Hint: Dividend=@P1_Values[@R_i@]@, Divisor=@P2_Values[@R_i@]@)",

      "temperature": "0.4",

      "max-tokens": "2000",

      "show": false,

      "model": "gpt-4.1-nano"

    },

    {

      "system": "@JSON_PARSER_PERSONA@",

      "user": "@TR@TN(-1)@[@R_i@]@",

      "temperature": "0.1",

      "max-tokens": "2000",

      "show": false,

      "model": "gpt-4.1-nano"

    },

    {

      "system": "",

      "user": "/ T4 (LOOP 3/5): Store the clean JSON from T3 into a unique JP for this item.\\n@SETJ(Item_@R_i@_Distractors, @TR@TN(-1)@[@R_i@]@)@",

      "show": false,

      "model": null

    },

    {

      "system": "",

      "user": "/ T5 (LOOP 4/5): Extract distractor values from the JP using JSONVALS.\\n@SET(DISTRACTOR_VALUES_@R_i@, \"@JSONVALS(Item_@R_i@_Distractors, \"Distractor\")@\")@",

      "show": false,

      "model": null

    },

    {

      "system": "",

      "user": "/ T6 (LOOP 5/5): Assemble the final JSON string, using @D() to create 6 choices (1 correct + 5 distractors).\\n{\"identifier\":\"Item_@R_i@\", \"prompt\":\"@Stem_Feature[@R_i@]@\", \"choices\":\"@D(\"@Answer_Feature[@R_i@]@\", \"\", \"@DISTRACTOR_VALUES_@R_i@@\", \"6\", \"ASCE\")@\", \"correctAnswer\":\"@Answer_Feature[@R_i@]@\", \"distractor_data\":@Item_@R_i@_Distractors@}",

      "show": true,

      "model": null

    },

      "temperature": "0.1",

      "max-tokens": "4000",

      "show": true,

      "model": "gpt-4.1-nano"

    },

    {

      "system": "",

      "show": false,

      "model": null

    },

      "show": false,

      "model": null

    },

    {

      "system": "",

      "user": "/ T10 (LOOP 1/3): Display each item from the 'assessmentTest' JSON array for validation.\\n@RADIO(R_@R_i@, \"@assessmentTest[@R_i@].prompt@\", \"@assessmentTest[@R_i@].choices@\")@",

      "show": true,

      "model": null

    },

    {

      "system": "",

      "user": "/ T11 (LOOP 2/3): Grade the user's response.\\n@SET(RESULT_TEXT_@R_i@, \"@MAP(\"@RADIO(R_@R_i@)@\", \"@assessmentTest[@R_i@].correctAnswer@\", \"Correct|Incorrect\")@\")@",

      "show": false,

      "model": null

    },

    {

      "system": "",

      "user": "/ T12 (LOOP 3/3): Display the feedback and 5-distractor analysis.\\n## Result for Item @R_i@\\n\\n- **Your Answer:** @RADIO(R_@R_i@)@\\n- **Correct Answer:** @assessmentTest[@R_i@].correctAnswer@\\n- **Grade:** @RESULT_TEXT_@R_i@@\\n\\n### Distractor Analysis\\n| Distractor | Rationale (Common Error) |\\n| :--- | :--- |\\n| @assessmentTest[@R_i@].distractor_data[0].Distractor@ | @assessmentTest[@R_i@].distractor_data[0].Rationale@ |\\n| @assessmentTest[@R_i@].distractor_data[1].Distractor@ | @assessmentTest[@R_i@].distractor_data[1].Rationale@ |\\n| @assessmentTest[@R_i@].distractor_data[2].Distractor@ | @assessmentTest[@R_i@].distractor_data[2].Rationale@ |\\n| @assessmentTest[@R_i@].distractor_data[3].Distractor@ | @assessmentTest[@R_i@].distractor_data[3].Rationale@ |\\n| @assessmentTest[@R_i@].distractor_data[4].Distractor@ | @assessmentTest[@R_i@].distractor_data[4].Rationale@ |\\n",

      "show": true,

      "markdown": true,

      "model": null

    }

  ]

}

  

## Detailed Logic Breakdown

### Ontology Model (options.params)

- Stem_Feature (SHUFFLE): Primary stem list; drives instance ordering.
    
- Answer_Feature (LINK(Stem_Feature)): Correct answers remain aligned with stems after shuffle.
    
- P1_Values / P2_Values (LINK(Stem_Feature)): Parallel numeric features used to hint the LLM for more realistic distractor generation.
    
- DISTRACTOR_GENERATOR_PERSONA: System persona for Turn 2 enforcing exactly five rows in a Markdown table.
    
- JSON_PARSER_PERSONA: System persona for Turn 3 enforcing strict JSON array output with five objects.
    
- numberOfInstances: Governs generation count and validation loop count.
    

### Execution Flow (prompts array)

- Turn 1 (Symbolic): Generation loop setup  
    REPEAT executes Turns 2–6 for each item instance.
    
- Turn 2 (LLM): Generate distractors in Markdown  
    LLM creates a 2-column Markdown table (Distractor, Rationale), exactly five rows.
    
- Turn 3 (LLM): Parse Markdown → JSON  
    LLM converts the table into a strict JSON array of five objects.
    
- Turn 4 (Symbolic): Store per-item distractor JSON  
    SETJ writes the parsed JSON into a unique JSON Parameter: Item_i_Distractors.
    
- Turn 5 (Symbolic): Extract only distractor values  
    JSONVALS pulls the Distractor field into a pipe-separated AP list for choice assembly.
    
- Turn 6 (Symbolic): Assemble final item JSON string  
    D() combines 1 correct answer + 5 distractors into 6 choices and embeds the full JSON distractor_data.
    
- Turn 7 (LLM): Compile all items into JSON array  
    Formatting utility LLM wraps concatenated item strings into a valid JSON array.
    
- Turn 8 (Symbolic): Store assessmentTest artifact  
    SETJ saves the final array for administration/validation.
    
- Turn 9 (Symbolic): Validation loop setup  
    REPEAT runs Turns 10–12 for each item in assessmentTest.
    
- Turn 10 (Symbolic): Deliver item  
    RADIO renders prompt and 6 choices.
    
- Turn 11 (Symbolic): Grade  
    MAP compares chosen response vs correct answer and stores a correctness label.
    
- Turn 12 (Symbolic): Diagnostic feedback  
    Displays grade and a 5-row distractor rationale table by indexing distractor_data[0..4].
